text:
NATIONAL
POLICE
OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS BRIEFING
UPDATE ON INVESTIGATION OF THE FATAL SHOOTING OF
HON. CHARLES ONG'ONDO WERE
The National Police Service wishes to provide a comprehensive
update on the ongoing investigation into the tragic murder of Hon.
Charles Ong'ondo Were, Member of Parliament for Kasipul, which
occurred on April 30, 2025.
At approximately 7:40 PM on April 30, 2025, Hon. Charles Were was
fatally shot while driving in a white Toyota Crown along Ngong Road,
near the City Mortuary roundabout in Nairobi. The vehicle had
stopped at a red traffic light when a motorcycle carrying a rider and
a pillion passenger pulled alongside. The pillion passenger
approached the passenger's side of the vehicle, fired multiple shots,
and fled the scene on the motorcycle. The driver and the bodyguard,
both unharmed, rushed Hon. Were to Nairobi Hospital, where he was
pronounced dead on arrival.
A specialised team from the DCI Homicide Bureau, supported by
forensic experts from the National Forensic Laboratory, was promptly
deployed to the crime scene. The team conducted a thorough
examination, collecting critical evidence that has significantly
advanced the investigation. Detectives reconstructed Hon. Were's
movements from Parliament to the site of the shooting, generating
key leads that have helped identify potential suspects. The driver and
the bodyguard were taken into custody to assist in the ongoing probe.
---
On May 2, 2025 an autopsy was conducted at Lee Funeral Home by
Dr. Johansen Oduor. Chief Government Pathologist, in the presence
of the Director of Homicide Investigations, forensic experts, family
members, legal counsel, and representatives from Parliament. The
examination revealed that Hon. Were sustained five gunshot wounds,
all entering from the left side of his body. Two bullets were recovered
during the autopsy, and a third was found in the deceased's vehicle.
These exhibits were submitted for ballistic analysis.
Other exhibits collected at the initial stages of the investigation
include: Surveillance footage capturing critical moments before and
after the incident, Identification of a vehicle used to transport the
suspects to the crime scene and financial proceeds linked to the
suspects. These exhibits are undergoing forensic analysis to further
strengthen the case and clarify the circumstances surrounding Hon.
Were's murder.
Through meticulous forensic work, four suspects directly linked to
the crime scene were arrested. Some of them are believed to be
members of the "Mjahidini," an organised criminal gang known for
armed robberies in Nairobi's Eastlands area. On May 5, 2025, the
four suspects were presented before the JKIA Court, where
investigators secured a 30-day custodial order to facilitate further
inquiries. The case is scheduled for mention on June 5, 2025.
Two additional suspects have been apprehended. Following their
arrest, the two led investigators to a residence where key evidence
was recovered, including two firearms: A Retay Falcon pistol and a
Sarsilmaz pistol, a bag and footwear matching descriptions of items
worn by one of the suspects at the crime scene. All recovered items
were submitted for forensic examination.
Furthermore, two more key suspects were arrested yesterday,
bringing the number of suspects in custody to ten.
---
Today I stand before you with significant findings from a
comprehensive ballistic investigation regarding the tragic demise of
Hon. Charles Were. The ballistic report we have received
unequivocally links the Sarsilmaz pistol, recovered from the
residence of one of the suspects, to the fatal shots that took his life.
This critical piece of evidence not only identifies the weapon used in
this heinous act but also reveals its involvement in a series of other
criminal activities. Specifically, the same firearm has been implicated
in three separate robbery incidents across Nairobi and Kiambu
Counties, with the most recent crime occurring on April 26, 2025.
This progress demonstrates the NPS's commitment to resolving this
case with the highest standards of professionalism and diligence. We
will continue to pursue all leads, analyse forensic evidence, and
ensure that all perpetrators are brought to justice.
We are grateful for the cooperation of Hon. Were's family, friends, and
members of the public, whose valuable information has driven
significant progress in this investigation.
We urge anyone with additional information to contact their nearest
police station or use our toll-free lines: 999, 112, or #FichuaKwaDCI
(0800 722 203). All information provided will be treated with utmost
confidentiality.
As I conclude, I want to assure all Kenyans that we are committed to
pursuing this investigation with the utmost diligence to ensure that
all those involved are brought to justice. Further updates will be
provided as the investigation progresses.
DOUGLAS KANJA KIROCHO, MGH, CBS, OGW
INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
May 8, 2025

OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS STATEMENT
National Police Service Headquarters
For Immediate Release
UPDATE FOLLOWING ATTACKS AT KEUMBU, KISII COUNTY
The National Police Service (NPS) wishes to update the public on the ongoing
investigation into a video circulating in mainstream and social media, which
depicts an attack on a convoy of motor vehicles.
Further analysis has established that the incident occurred along the Kisii-
Keroka road on Friday, 3rd July 2026, and targeted a political group present in
the area.
In response, officers from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Kisii
Central, and Keumbu Police Station moved swiftly and arrested three suspects,
who are currently in custody.
A more detailed analysis of the video, alongside wider investigative efforts, is
underway with a view to making further arrests.
The NPS strongly condemns the events depicted. Political intolerance, in
whatever form, is unacceptable and will be rigorously pursued through the
criminal justice system.
The Inspector General of the National Police Service (IG-NPS) has directed the
Internal Affairs Unit (IAU) to expedite its assessment of all aspects of the violence,
identify any operational gaps that may have contributed to the incident, and take
appropriate action within the broader context of the attack. IAU officers are
already on the ground in the affected area.
The NPS further appeals for the public's continued support and encourages
anyone with information relating to this incident to share it patriotically with the
nearest police station, or via the toll-free numbers 999, 911, or 0800 722 203
(FichuakwaDCI), or through WhatsApp on 0709 570 000.
As a Service, we remain committed to protecting the public, investigating all
cases to their logical conclusion, and ensuring that perpetrators are brought to
justice.
MUCHRI-NYAGA
DIRECTOR CORPORATE COMMUNICATION/SPOKESPERSON
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
July 4, 2026
End

NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
Telegrams: "CRIMINAL" Nairobi
Email: director @cid.go.ke
MAZINGIRA HOUSE
KIAMBU ROAD
P.O. Box 30036
Tel: 020343312, 0202603724.
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
PRESS STATEMENT
UPDATE ON INVESTIGATIONS INTO CRIMINAL ACTIVITIES EXPERIENCED DURING
THE JUNE 25, 2025 PROTESTS
1. In a press address on June 24, 2025, the Inspector General of the National Police
Service urged those Kenyans who were organising and those planning to participate
in the demonstrations the following day Wednesday, June 25, 2025, to do so within
the confines of the law. He emphasised the importance of maintaining order during
these protests and pledged the full support of the police in ensuring the safety of all
participants. The Inspector General reassured citizens that their right to peaceful
assembly, as enshrined in Article 37 of the Constitution, would be upheld and that
law enforcement would facilitate a secure environment for the exercise of their rights.
2. On Wednesday, June 25, 2025, Kenya witnessed demonstrations dubbed the
Gen-Z anniversary protests. While some citizens turned out peacefully to exercise
their constitutional right to assemble and express dissent; a well-coordinated network
of criminal actors infiltrated and hijacked these demonstrations. These criminals came
out with the sole intention to cause chaos, loot, destroy lives and property with a clear,
coordinated agenda to forcibly enter lawfully protected areas and destroy government
installations.
---
3. We acknowledge, with deep sorrow, that these events resulted in the loss of lives.
We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families who have, unfortunately and
regrettably, lost their loved ones. Law enforcement officers suffered significant harm
while protecting genuine protestors, property and maintain law and order, with at
least eleven officers sustaining serious injuries, some life-threatening. Every life lost
is a tragedy that shakes the conscience of the nation. We mourn with you, and we
remain committed to ensuring that justice is not only done but is seen to be done.
No family should ever suffer such pain under the pretence of protest or the breakdown
of public order.
4. We confirm that what began as peaceful civic action in certain parts of the
country quickly devolved into orchestrated violence. Intelligence and arrest records
reveal that some individuals with specific instructions to attack public institutions and
security installations were ferried in unmarked vehicles from particular areas that
security agencies are currently looking into.
5. Our investigations have unearthed a series of deeply troubling incidents. There
was widespread destruction of critical government infrastructure, such as Kikuyu
Law Courts, Kikuyu County Government Offices, and multiple police stations,
including Olkalau Police Station, Dagoretti, Gachui, and Kamukunji, among others.
6. Several firearms and police equipment were stolen during these attacks, and
disturbingly, some of these weapons have already been used in violent robberies
within Naivasha region. A grenade launcher, four guns and other police equipment
including uniforms and anti-riot gear stolen have so far been recovered and the
perpetrators apprehended.
7.
Businesses, both public and private, were not spared. Notably, several wholesale
and retail outlets in Nairobi CBD, Kitengela, Dagoreti, Naivasha, Kikuyu, Nyeri among
others were brazenly looted and vandalized. Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) were
violently broken into, and millions of shillings were stolen in the chaos. In addition,
we received credible reports of assault and sexual violence committed by criminals
---
who had earlier infiltrated the demonstrations, further compounding the gravity of
the situation.
8. On June 26, 2025, the Ndunyu Njeru police station in North Kinangop Sub-
county experienced a violent incident, where approximately 400 armed individuals
stormed the facility demanding the release of four prisoners arrested for stock theft
earlier that day. Despite the officers' resistance, the crowd overwhelmed them,
resulting in the burning of the police station and the tragic suffocation and deaths of
three suspects, whereas one is currently hospitalised in a very critical condition. This
incident, while not directly linked to the events of June 25, reflects the ongoing
momentum of violence against police stations in the country, a trend that continues
to threaten law and order and jeopardise our nation's peace and security. Fellow
Kenyans, we must not allow our nation to spiral into anarchy and chaos; the police
will not remain passive while lawlessness threatens our collective peace and security.
9.
As of today, 485 individuals have been arrested in connection to these incidents.
Of these, 448 have already been charged in court, and 37 remain under active
investigation, some pending further custodial hearings. The charges range from
murder, terrorism, rape, gang rape, arson, obstruction of police officers on duty,
breaking and stealing, robbery, robbery with violence, stealing from locked motor
vehicles, incitement to violence, handling stolen goods, malicious damage to property,
and possession of illegal firearms.
10. Preliminary investigations, including statements obtained from these arrested
suspects, reveal a deliberate and well-funded plot to incite chaos, civil unrest, and
widespread anarchy under the guise of public protest. Evidence indicates that
individuals were strategically mobilized and transported particularly into Nairobi
from various parts of the country, not to express legitimate grievances, but to execute
a coordinated agenda of disruption and violence.
---
11. These actions were not spontaneous; they were orchestrated. We are actively
pursuing the key planners, mobilizers, financiers, and facilitators behind this scheme,
and they will be brought to justice.
12. The complaints we have received from across the country draw a clear and
troubling line between lawful protest and outright criminality. While some youthful
protestors joined the demonstrations in good faith, some individuals tragically, even
some who had marched peacefully, later turned on fellow Kenyans.
13. They engaged in sexual violence, theft and broke into homes and businesses.
Such acts not only violated the law but also betrayed the very ideals the protests
purported to uphold. When demonstrations descend into violence, intimidation, and
the destruction of property, they do not advance any cause, they discredit it. They
erode public sympathy and distort the message of those who genuinely seek reform
through lawful and constructive means.
14. It must be clearly understood that the right to protest is protected under our
Constitution, and we respect the voice of every Kenyan seeking accountability and
reform. However, when a bonafide protest is infiltrated by criminal elements, it
becomes a threat to national security and public safety.
15. We commend those who protested peacefully and distanced themselves from
acts of lawlessness. Some among them became victims themselves attacked, robbed,
or assaulted by those who took advantage of the crowd.
16. To those who orchestrated, funded and mobilized the undermining of genuine
protests, your actions are an assault to the exercise of the sovereign power of the
people of Kenya. It has not gone unnoticed, and as you will be swiftly held
accountable.
17. We call upon members of the public to continue sharing information that leads
to the tracking of stolen firearms, stolen goods from businesses, apprehension of
suspects, and to restore normalcy in the affected areas.

escape from the forest where he was already
undergoing forced fasting and was hosted for
the night by a well-wisher who took him to
the area chief, and later Malindi police station.
The boy subsequently led members of the
initial investigating team back to the forest,
where he identified several graves and also
drew a sketch plan showing how the forest

with biblical names such as Tiro, Bethlehem,

During one of the burials that Mackenzie
was presiding over, he announced to the
congregants that adults would start fasting
to death immediately after the death of their
children. As a result, adults both men and
women whose children had died commenced
fasting. Some relocated from their residences
to deep in the forest, to fast to death. This was
to avoid breaking the fast and detection by
the outsiders who had started accessing the
forest. Homicide detectives investigating the
mass killings discovered that adults were also
forced to starve.
This is because during the rescue exercise,

been surrounded by a group of four men
watching over them. Correspondingly, men
who had been assigned security duties to
prevent the devotees from escaping guarded
those fasting in makeshift fasting bays. This
indicated that they were not on voluntary

When children started dying as a result of the
forced fasting, they would initially be buried
outside their parents' homesteads in shallow
pits and traditional vegetables planted on
the flattened surface to conceal them. In a
move that deprived the dead an opportunity
for a dignified send off in accordance with
one's traditional and religious beliefs, the
remains of Mackenzie's followers would be
shoved into the hurriedly prepared pits and
covered under a heap of soil, without giving
the bereaved a period to mourn. The dead
bodies would either be wrapped in a bed
sheet, blanket or leso, or buried in an exercise
spearheaded by Mackenzie or his assistants
Evans, Steve, or Julius. This fact was confirmed
and observed during the exhumation
exercises, as none of the exhumed bodies
was found in a coffin but only wrapped in
either bed sheets, blankets, shawls or lesos.
Some bodies also had their legs tied together
using ropes or pieces of clothing, supposedly
for ease of transportation to burial sites. As

The DCI EXPERT OPINION
A
notification came to our office at the Division of Forensic
and Pathology Service (The Division), Ministry of health.
It was in form of a letter from Directorate of Criminal
Investigations (the DCI). In this letter, the DCI requested
for support from The Division following a report that there were two
children who had been buried in a shallow grave at Chakama Ranch,
Shaka Hola. They requested for our support in form of exhumation
and post mortem in order to establish what caused their death. There
were also reports that the deaths could be linked to harmful religious
practices. Accompanying the letter was an exhumation order from the
court. Having been involved in many exhumation exercises before, we
thought that it was a simple exercise and it was our hope that within
the less than a week, we will be through with the whole process.
A team of dedicated officers comprising of a
driver, two senior pathologists and a senior
forensic odontology was quickly mobilised.
Such exercises have always generated a lot of
excitement in The Division due to different
challenges encountered by the officers and
the lessons learnt from uniqueness of each
case. It was therefore easy to mobilise the
team, even before completion the logistics
of getting them their Daily Subsistence
Allowance (DSA). Within no time the team
was on its way to Malindi by road. Upon
reaching Malindi, the team went straight to
the site of incidence and that is where we
uncounted the shocking reality.
The surprise
The area was bushy and off the main road
from Malindi to Tsavo National Park. Upon
leaving the tarmacked road, the team drove
for a few kilometres until the vehicles could
go no further due to difficult terrain. The
team had to disembark from the Landcruiser
ferrying and cover the remaining 5 kilometres
on foot. This was coupled by the high temperature in the area and fear
of encountering wild animals including elephants and serpents. Woe
unto those who were unfit and had a phobia for walking alongside
wild animals! Upon reaching the site, instead of the two cases that the
team had gone to exhume and perform post mortem examination on,
it emerged that there were mass graves within the expansive farm,
whose number could not be determined at that time (by the time of
writing this article, the team had performed a total of 429 autopsies,
with reports of there being more graves). This meant that the scope
of the operation had to be upscaled, using a multi-agency approach.
There was also need to mobilise resources in order to undertake the
operation to keep with international standards, the standards that we
had already established during our past exercises, with this case giving
us an opportunity to learn and make more improvement.
The exhumation processes
The exhumation process involves use of various teams in a coordinated
fashion the team exhumed bodes that has been buried in shallow
graves. They included male and female adults, children, infants.
In some instances, the team found several bodies buried in a single
grave. There were homesteads that had been abandoned and had
graves therein (possibly containing the owners of the homesteads).
There were many challenges encountered including accessibility to
the areas where the graves were (this was addressed by the county
government of Kilifi making roads for ease of access), extremes of
weather (periods of scorching sun alternating with heavy rains) and
the fact that the area was remote with no shops so that once in the
ranch, you were stuck there the whole day until the end of the day's
activities. Thank for P.C. Masese and Juliet, we were well nourished
due to their cooking skills. (Pojo na wali).
Apart from the exhumations, there were officers who were combing
the area to rescue the victims who were still alive. Some were found
in the verge of dying from starvation and severe dehydration. Some
were found dead in bushes. There were groups a of people who were
reported to be escaping deeper into the forest and a team from the
police force pursued them in order to rescue them. The exhumation
process was done in phases whereby in one phase, all identified graves

Chief Government Pathologist Dr Johansen Oduor, compare notes. PHOTO/COURTESY

one team was performing post mortem, there was a team which was
working it the field identifying graves, in readiness for the neck phase
of exhumation.
The post mortem examination
process
Post mortem examinations were performed at Malindi subcounty
hospital mortuary. We divided ourselves into 3 group, each group
comprising of pathologists, morticians, crime scene officers,
investigating officer and staff from the government chemist. There
were also officers the human rights organisations including Kenya
National Commission for Human Rights and Haki Afrika overseeing
the whole process.
initially there. At one point, Director of Homicide (Martin Nyuguto)
rushed to our autopsy room upon hearing a Gikuyu song that he last
heard while courting his wife. It was indeed an elating moment. To
take care of our mental health, there was a psychologist at hand who
was giving us group and individual debriefing sessions.
The conclusion
The exercise is still ongoing. There have been many lessons learnt,
especially multiagency approach to disasters. The government is also
very supportive, with the frequent visits from The Cabinet Secretary
of Interior and Administration of National government, Prof. Kithura
Kindiki, who gave us words of encouragement, thus boosting the
morale of the team.
We also have overwhelming support from the Ministry of Health who
have treated all our requests with utmost urgency.
The exercise has also brought out the hidden potentials and skills of
everyone in the team, with The Director of Homicide ensuring that
he is out there in the bush every day and at times taking up the jembe
and personally digging the graves. There are also my colleagues like
Dr. Njeru and Dr. Nyamunga who have unleashed their gifts of hard
work, resilience and attention to details. The Morticians too who have
worked hard without any complains. No one in the team has let us
down!
It is our hope that we will be able to exhume all bodies and ensure that
justice is served using our evidence.
MBChB (UoN), Mmed Path (UoN), LLB Hons (UoN)Dip For Med
(CMSA), Head Division of Forensic Medicine, Ministry of Health/
Chief Government Pathologist
The mortuary, being small was unable to accommodate the whole
process. One of our partners, International Committee of the Red Dr. Oduor Johansen
Cross (ICRC) donated two mobile refrigerators to help in storage of
the bodies. During the post mortem, the stench from decomposing
bodies was overwhelming. Our noses progressively adapted to it
though not to a great extent. The high temperatures in Malindi meant
that as we were working, we were getting easily dehydrated thus need
for frequent breaks to rehydrate ourselves. PC Masese and Juliet were
also on standby once again, ensuring that none of us die of starvation.
There were also light moments. Being a Luo (Jaluo Very Complicated),
I came with a JBL. speaker which was entertaining us as we work.
Chepchieng', too was at hand showing us his dancing skills, skills he
had acquired in his long service as a police officer while working in
different parts of our republic. Dr. Mercy also showed us her skills of
singing along Bongo music. All this elevated the sombre mood that was

The DCI
OPINIONS
Report & Photos by
Edwin Kipkorir
Shakahola Residents Living in Fear of Isolation from Society
Following the death of over 420 people in the Shakahola cult killings, the DCI
Magazine's editorial team toured various parts of Kilifi County and spoke to
ordinary Kenyans seeking their views on how the mass deaths had affected
their lives. Below are some of their views as captured by Police Constable
Edwin Kipkorir.
Changawa Mangi Yaa
Village Elder, Shakahola
Mackenzie
came
alone, but within a
short time, there were
very many people.
We were told that
they were followers
of
Mackenzie's
church but they were
shocked that they
didn't want to interact
with us. Upon arrival,
the cult members
were healthy and
they would troop
to our shopping
centre to buy
foodstuff. Business
was booming in this
trading centre as the
cult members would
buy goods in bulk.
However, with time the cult members started losing weight
and when we asked we were told that they were starving at the
shrine. Children began escaping from the forest and I hosted
several of them who said that they were being forced to fast
and if you didn't, Mackenzie's aides beat you up. I remember
a 13 year-old boy whom I hosted was so malnourished that he
would pass stool full of soil which he had eaten due to lack of
food. That is when we started realizing that all was not well at
Shakahola kwa Mackenzie. I set off for the forest to find out
what was happening but Mackenzie's men who were armed
with machetes set ablaze our motorbike and ejected us from the
forest. The shame that Mackenzie has brought us in Shakahola
cannot be expressed in words. People from all over the world
now think that Shakahola is a church where we starve children
to death yet we are a patriotic and God fearing people who go
about our business peacefully.
Karisa Chalo
Plant Operator, Malindi
I had gone to Shakahola forest
in the company of Changawa
Mangi from the Wamwabaya
Mwaro clan among others,
for a demarcation exercise
of a piece of land that I had
jointly acquired with a group
of 45 people. We had bought
500 acres of land at over Sh2.5
million and had gone to plant
beacons on the piece of land.
On our way out of the forest,
we heard faint howls and
yowls similar to those of a cat,
coming from a thicket a few
metres away. We continued
walking then all of a sudden,
we heard shaky voices of
distress tusaidieni, tusaidieni
(please help us, come to
our aid)! We stopped and
turned towards the direction of the distress calls when we saw about four
emaciated women, lying on what appeared to be a mat spread under a tree
canopy pleading for assistance. As we surged forward to assist the women,
we spotted a group of men armed with machetes and other crude weapons
watching over them. The men charged towards us and we scampered
for safety towards the main road. I reported the matter to police and the
following day, accompanied them to the forest.
The images of the emaciated women I saw that day still linger in my mind to
date. I keep having nightmares and wish that I had known of the situation
earlier, since I would have saved more lives.

graves. They included male and female adults, children, infants.
In some instances, the team found several bodies buried in a single
grave. There were homesteads that had been abandoned and had
graves therein (possibly containing the owners of the homesteads).
There were many challenges encountered including accessibility to
the areas where the graves were (this was addressed by the county
government of Kilifi making roads for ease of access), extremes of
weather (periods of scorching sun alternating with heavy rains) and
the fact that the area was remote with no shops so that once in the
ranch, you were stuck there the whole day until the end of the day's
activities. Thank for P.C. Masese and Juliet, we were well nourished
due to their cooking skills. (Pojo na wali).
Apart from the exhumations, there were officers who were combing
the area to rescue the victims who were still alive. Some were found
in the verge of dying from starvation and severe dehydration. Some
were found dead in bushes. There were groups a of people who were
reported to be escaping deeper into the forest and a team from the
police force pursued them in order to rescue them. The exhumation
process was done in phases whereby in one phase, all identified graves

process
Post mortem examinations were performed at Malindi subcounty
hospital mortuary. We divided ourselves into 3 group, each group
comprising of pathologists, morticians, crime scene officers,

were also officers the human rights organisations including Kenya

take care of our mental health, there was a psychologist at hand who
was giving us group and individual debriefing sessions.
The conclusion
The exercise is still ongoing. There have been many lessons learnt,
especially multiagency approach to disasters. The government is also
very supportive, with the frequent visits from The Cabinet Secretary
of Interior and Administration of National government, Prof. Kithura
Kindiki, who gave us words of encouragement, thus boosting the
morale of the team.
We also have overwhelming support from the Ministry of Health who
have treated all our requests with utmost urgency.
The exercise has also brought out the hidden potentials and skills of
everyone in the team, with The Director of Homicide ensuring that
he is out there in the bush every day and at times taking up the jembe
and personally digging the graves. There are also my colleagues like
Dr. Njeru and Dr. Nyamunga who have unleashed their gifts of hard
work, resilience and attention to details. The Morticians too who have
worked hard without any complains. No one in the team has let us
down!
It is our hope that we will be able to exhume all bodies and ensure that
justice is served using our evidence.

Shakahola Residents Living in Fear of Isolation from Society
Following the death of over 420 people in the Shakahola cult killings, the DCI
Magazine's editorial team toured various parts of Kilifi County and spoke to
ordinary Kenyans seeking their views on how the mass deaths had affected
their lives. Below are some of their views as captured by Police Constable
Edwin Kipkorir.
Changawa Mangi Yaa
Village Elder, Shakahola
Mackenzie
came
alone, but within a
short time, there were
very many people.
We were told that
they were followers
of
Mackenzie's
church but they were
shocked that they
didn't want to interact
with us. Upon arrival,
the cult members
were healthy and
they would troop
to our shopping
centre to buy
foodstuff. Business
was booming in this
trading centre as the
cult members would
buy goods in bulk.
However, with time the cult members started losing weight
and when we asked we were told that they were starving at the
shrine. Children began escaping from the forest and I hosted
several of them who said that they were being forced to fast
and if you didn't, Mackenzie's aides beat you up. I remember
a 13 year-old boy whom I hosted was so malnourished that he
would pass stool full of soil which he had eaten due to lack of
food. That is when we started realizing that all was not well at
Shakahola kwa Mackenzie. I set off for the forest to find out
what was happening but Mackenzie's men who were armed
with machetes set ablaze our motorbike and ejected us from the
forest. The shame that Mackenzie has brought us in Shakahola
cannot be expressed in words. People from all over the world
now think that Shakahola is a church where we starve children
to death yet we are a patriotic and God fearing people who go
about our business peacefully.
Karisa Chalo
Plant Operator, Malindi
I had gone to Shakahola forest
in the company of Changawa
Mangi from the Wamwabaya
Mwaro clan among others,
for a demarcation exercise
of a piece of land that I had
jointly acquired with a group
of 45 people. We had bought
500 acres of land at over Sh2.5
million and had gone to plant
beacons on the piece of land.
On our way out of the forest,
we heard faint howls and
yowls similar to those of a cat,
coming from a thicket a few
metres away. We continued
walking then all of a sudden,
we heard shaky voices of
distress tusaidieni, tusaidieni
(please help us, come to
our aid)! We stopped and
turned towards the direction of the distress calls when we saw about four
emaciated women, lying on what appeared to be a mat spread under a tree
canopy pleading for assistance. As we surged forward to assist the women,
we spotted a group of men armed with machetes and other crude weapons
watching over them. The men charged towards us and we scampered
for safety towards the main road. I reported the matter to police and the
following day, accompanied them to the forest.
The images of the emaciated women I saw that day still linger in my mind to
date. I keep having nightmares and wish that I had known of the situation
earlier, since I would have saved more lives.

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
PRESS RELEASE
INVESTIGATIONS INTO THE REPORTED DISAPPEARANCE OF HON. RAPHAEL TUJU
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) has launched investigations into the
reported disappearance of Hon. Raphael Tuju following a missing person report
lodged at Karen Police Station.
Hon. Tuju was reported missing by his family on Sunday, March 22, 2026. His motor
vehicle was discovered abandoned along Miotoni Lane in Karen, with its hazard lights
on. A security guard from a nearby institution alerted authorities, prompting a swift
response by officers from Karen Police Station. The scene was later processed by
Crime Scene Investigators and the vehicle towed to Karen Police Station for further
forensic examination.
Efforts to reach Hon. Tuju have so far been unsuccessful, as his mobile phone remains
switched off. A specialized team has since been deployed to handle the case and is
working in coordination with all other relevant government agencies to establish his
whereabouts. The investigating team is also utilizing all available resources and
investigative techniques to determine the circumstances surrounding his reported
disappearance.
While progress is being made, the DCI notes that an attempt by investigators to access
Mr. Tuju's residence along Mwitu Drive was denied by the family. We urge full
cooperation from all parties, including unrestricted access to relevant locations and
prompt provision of information, for a swift and thorough resolution.
Members of the public who may have information regarding Hon. Tuju's
whereabouts, or who may have seen him, his vehicle, or any suspicious activity in the
Miotoni Lane or greater Karen area before, on or after March 21, 2026, are also
urged to come forward. Information may be shared confidentially through DCI Toll-
Free Line: 0800 722 222, WhatsApp 0709 570 000 to report anonymously or to the
nearest police station.
The investigation remains ongoing and further updates will be provided as significant
developments arise.
JOHN MARETE, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
March 22, 2026

text:
NATIONAL
POLICE
SERVICE
UPDATE ON
OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS BRIEFING
THE INVESTIGATION INTO THE ALLEGED
ABDUCTION OF HON. GEORGE KOIMBURI
The National Police Service (NPS) wishes to provide a
comprehensive update on the ongoing investigation into the
alleged abduction of Hon. George Koimburi, Member of Parliament
for Juja Constituency.
On Monday, 26 May 2025, the attention of the National Police
Service was drawn to an amateur video circulating on social and
mainstream media, purportedly showing the Member of
Parliament abandoned at a farm in Juja.
Police officers from Juja swiftly responded, visiting the alleged
scene and thoroughly documenting the area. Upon comparing the
vegetation and road dimensions at the scene with those in the
video, it was established that the two did not match. During
questioning, Moses Kariuki, the caretaker of the coffee farm which
is owned by one Jimmy Wanjigi, stated that he had not witnessed
such an incident.
The officers then proceeded to Plainview Hospital in Ruiru, where
the Member of Parliament had reportedly been taken for treatment.
They confirmed that the vehicle used to transport him registration
number KCJ 660P belonged to Hon. George Koimburi and was
driven by Frida Njeri, who was also the first responder at the
alleged crime scene. The hospital did not disclose the nature of the
treatment or first aid administered, making it difficult to assess
the extent of the alleged injuries.
Meanwhile, a specialised team from the DCI Headquarters,
supported by forensic experts from the National Forensic
Laboratory, was promptly deployed to the scene to conduct a
thorough examination, gather critical evidence, and establish the
circumstances surrounding these allegations.
---
To date, the investigating team has interviewed and recorded
statements from five individuals, with several more expected to
provide their accounts and particularly Hon. George Koimburi,
whom we shall interview at the earliest opportunity after his family
objected to our attempts to reach him.
This progress underscores the NPS's commitment to uncovering
the truth regarding the abduction allegations with the highest
standards of professionalism and diligence. We will continue to
pursue all leads, analyse forensic evidence, and ensure that any
perpetrators are brought to justice.
Additionally, it is important to note that Hon. George Koimburi has
been under investigation for a land fraud case, and the Office of
the Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) had already issued
consent for his prosecution.
On Friday, 23 May 2025, the MP fully aware of the police's
intention to arrest him evaded arrest by escaping on a motorcycle
with his private security and switched off his mobile phone. His
car, occupied only by his driver, was intercepted, and the driver
was arrested but later released after recording a statement. The
MP only resurfaced yesterday, coinciding with the abduction
claims.
We once again urge anyone with information regarding the
incident depicted in the video to report to their nearest police
station or contact us via our toll-free numbers: 999, 911, 112, or
#FichuakwaDCI (0800 722 203).
In conclusion, we assure all Kenyans that we are committed to
conducting this investigation with the utmost diligence to uncover
the truth behind these allegations. Further updates will be
provided as the investigation progresses.
DOUGLAS KANJA KIROCHO, MGH, CBS, OGW
INSPECTOR-GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
May 27, 2025
Ends

Sleuths Crippled

Foothold in the
Country
By Jonah Kimani

n September 12, 2024, Anti-
Narcotics Unit detectives in
Namanga received a tip-off about
a possible clandestine laboratory being set
up in a remote area within a 10-acre parcel
of land, 8 kilometres from the Nairobi-
Namanga highway. This was just a few
miles from the Kenya-Tanzania border.
The officers immediately set out on a
fact-finding mission to establish whether
the tip was solid. Indeed, the tip proved
credible, setting the foundation for the
detectives to disrupt a massive operation.
At first glance, the location indicated in the
tip didn't seem like much. The expansive
10-acre piece of land had only two iron
sheet structures. However, not being ones
to leave a stone unturned, the detectives
further investigated the structures.
Upon closer inspection, they found that
the iron sheet structures were cordoned
off using three tires and two cordon lines
of barbed wire. Moreover, the innermost
cordon was erected using iron sheets to
conceal the activities happening inside.
Besides the suspicious nature of the
structure, rumour had it that some foreign
nationals had been spotted moving in
and out of the site. At first, curious locals
assumed that a developer had bought
the land and were eager to secure job
opportunities once construction activities
began. However, their hopes dwindled
when only two relatively small iron
sheet structures were erected on
the 10-acre ranch. As time passed,
it became apparent to the locals that
no development project was underway
on the land. Yet, unbeknownst to them,
business was going on full-swing inside
the two unassuming structures; just not
the kind of business they expected.
On realizing they might have stumbled
into something beyond their purview,
Makeshift structures in Namanga that the
suspects used as clandestine meth labs for
their operations.

the Namanga team promptly roped
the DCI's specialized Anti-Narcotics
Directorate Unit into the investigation.
This was a necessary step to leverage
the Narcotics Unit's subject matter
expertise and to ensure proper handling
of evidence. Engaging the Anti-Narcotics
Unit informed the formation of a multi-
agency team comprising forensic analysts,
officers from the Government Chemist,
the Pharmacy and Poisons Board, Crime
Scene Investigators, and anti-drug
detectives, who would systematice"
process the scene to verify the claims.
True to the intelligence report, one of.
structures was found to house laboratory
apparatus (some of which were fully
mounted) and chemical substances,
while the other hosted a chemical store,
a kitchen, and a sleeping area. Based on
the evidence at the scene, including two
exercise books bearing lab drawings and
chemical formulas, a drug lab was being
set up.

Fortunately, the multiagency team found
one piece of evidence that would set the
stage for a thorough probe: a handset
abandoned at the scene. Thanks to this
crucial piece of evidence, they arrested
the first suspect in the suspected drug
syndicate only four days later.
The first suspect, Betty Mukami Micheni,
50, was arrested on September 16, 2024,
at her house in Ruiru, Kiambu County.
She was believed to have championed the
setting up of the lab, assisted by a second
suspect, Agwu Ojukwu, 51, a Nigerian
national.
During the arrest, the detectives recovered
several documents linking her to the
purchase, importation and distribution of
the land, chemicals and equipment found
at the scene in Namanga, at her residence.
Further analysis of the documents, money
trail, and communications revealed a
strong link between her and Agwu Ojukwu
and MBA, Agwu Ogba (also a Nigerian
national and a relative of Agwu Ojukwu).
A manhunt for the two
Nigerian nationals commenced,
culminating in the arrest of
51-year-old MBA, Ogwu Ogba,
on October 1, 2024, at his
house in Lavington, Nairobi.
Interestingly, Ogba posed
as a thrifted clothes vendor
struggling to survive in Nairobi,
despite his lifestyle in the affluent
leafy suburban neighbourhood
dotted with bistros, grills and
bars.
However, a closer look at MBA's
financials revealed a man of means. He
funded the field operations at the Namanga
site by sending loads of cash to Betty.
Moreover, MBA also owned a company
(Ngara Associate Investment Company)
and a fleet of transport trucks back in
Nigeria. He was also listed as a director in
a local Kenyan company.
Upon thorough interrogation, detectives
established that MBA's kin, Agwu
Ojukwu (alias Deacon or Pastor), was the
mastermind and architect of the entire
clandestine lab. They also learned that
MBA had just jetted into the country
on October 2 to assess the progress in
Namanga.
The DCI placed a stop order against
Ojukwu at Jomo Kenyatta International
Airport (JKIA), right on cue, to arrest him
on October 3 before he fled the country.
The culprit hardly left the airport when
word got to him that his associates in the
Namanga business were in police custody.
He attempted to book the next available
flight out of the country and escape the
hostile ground. Unfortunately for him, it
was too late.
On searching Ojukwu's luggage, police
discovered crucial pieces of evidence,
including the original land sale agreement
for the ranch in Namanga where the
temporary lab structures were erected.
The land sale agreement bore the name
of Ojukwu's alleged Kenyan wife as the
buyer. Also seized were copies of the
site's construction plan, a list of fencing
materials, a copy of the land title deed
from which the land was to be excised and
a handset.
Further investigations revealed Ojukwu
to be a multinational businessman who
visited Kenya for the first time in 2007,
allegedly for undisclosed business. Besides
owning multiple businesses in Nigeria,
Gabon, South Africa and China, he is also
linked to a drug cartel in South America.
He is also believed to be a gold smuggler
across the continent and beyond.
As investigations intensified, fingers
pointed to a fourth suspect, 41-year-old
Alvarado Israel Vera, a former member
of the Mexican Police's investigative unit.
Alvarado had arrived in the country
months earlier, alongside two other
compatriots, Carlos Pedro and Ignacio
Morales Alvarez. A stop order was also
placed against him and his crew at the
JKIA. He was arrested on October 5
during a botched attempt to escape back to
Mexico. His crew holed up.
Deeper inquiries into the case established
that Ojukwu had contracted the three
Mexicans for their expertise in 'cooking'
synthetic opioid (Methamphetamine). The
three Mexicans had spent several days at
the Namanga lab setting up the equipment
and receiving chemicals, as they were
tasked with guiding the facility's full
operationalisation.
On October 9, 2024, the police arrested
Caroline Wambui Muchira, 52, a
businesswoman, for her involvement in
coordinating with Ojukwu during the
purchase of the chemicals. A month later,
a sixth suspect, Francis Maina Gachau,
was also arrested in Juja. Maina was a
middleman involved in the distribution of

products. The police seized several forged
documents, including those bearing the
branding of renowned chemical business
companies, from Maina's house. Moreover,
some of the copies from Maina's house
matched those earlier found at the crime
scene in Namanga and in Betty Mukami's
(the first suspect) house in Kiambu.
The discovery informed the police's
decision to treat every company linked
to the clandestine lab as a lead. However,
by this time, all three suspects linked to
the lab in Namanga had been arrested

Also cited as defendants in the court were

To the untrained eye, the crackdown
seemed like just another local problem.
However, the extensive investigation
uncovered a powerful international
nexus spanning borders to Nigeria, India,
Mexico, South Africa, and Gabon.
International Links
Therefore, the DCI's
Anti-Narcotics
Unit had to call for reinforcement.
Thankfully, the DCI shares an established
cooperation partnership with the United
States Drug Enforcement Administration
(DEA). Consequently, DEA experts
visited the Namanga scene, particularly
when they learned of Alvarado Israel
Vera's Arrest. Moreover, they observed
that the clandestine lab bore uncanny
similarities to those set up by a notorious
South American drug cartel, operating
in Mexico. Having studied the lab, the
DEA concurred that Alvarado, Pedro and
Ignacio could only have been contracted
for one reason: establishing a clandestine
lab similar to those run by the cartel in
Mexico.
Second, the investigations established that
Betty, through her company BETLINK
SUPPLIES LTD, imported chemical
supplies from Indian-based companies,
including AADISH IMPEX PRIVET
COMPANY. The chemicals included
Sodium Hydroxide Flakes 98%, Tartaric
Acid GR 99%, Methylamine 40% and
Mercuric Chloride GR 99%
The chemicals highlighted above are
a highly-suspicious combination of
ingredients typically used in the illicit
manufacture of methamphetamine,
popularly known as crystal meth.
The American Addiction Centre describes
crystal meth as a highly addictive synthetic
stimulant with a high potential for misuse
and limited medical use. Most users
choose it for its relatively long-lasting
euphoric high. It is administered primarily
through smoking or direct injection into
the bloodstream.
Meth's immediate side effects include a
rapid heart rate, increased blood pressure,
increased respiratory rate, elevated body
temperature, insomnia, anxiety, aggression
and violence, tremors, convulsions,
cardiovascular issues such as stroke and
heart attack, death.
However, the illicit drug causes more
adverse long-term side effects, which
include delusions, chronic anxiety, visual
and auditory hallucinations, memory loss,
aggression and violent behaviour, Changes
in brain structure and function, paranoia,
severe dental problems, and in some cases
death by drug overdose.
Third, AGWU Ojukwu was also found
to be a South African resident who even
owned several businesses, including Kings
Lodge in North Cliff, Johannesburg.
The businesses are managed by his close
relative and are believed to be conduits for
laundering money. Besides South Africa,
Ojukwu also had ties to Libreville in
Gabon, where he'd established Jacome Ltd
Company, an entity that is also believed to
be a money-laundering conduit.
The attempt by such a dreaded internat
criminal enterprise to set up base in K
put the country on the spotlight over.

Narcotics Unit of the DCI was vindicated
when, in a brazen display of expertise and
speed, it managed to garner support from
multi-agency players and international
partners, rounding up the prime suspects
and arraigning them in court.
According to a March 2025 Drug and
Chemical Control report by the United
States Department of State Bureau
for International Narcotics and Law.
Enforcement Affairs, the drug problem
Kenya faced was significantly as a result of
its location on the East African coast, the
prime location as a gateway subjects the
country to exploitation by traffickers who
transit illicit drugs from Latin America
and Southwest Asia to Europe and the
Arabian Peninsula.
Also, the DEA established that Alvarado,
Pedro and Ignacio were members of
the Mexican Cartel de Jalisco Nueva
Generacion (CJNG). The CJNG is a

Moreover, the cartel was among eight

However, the 2024 discovery of a
clandestine lab is not the only incident that
has put Kenya in the spotlight regarding
narcotics. In the past years, massive drug
hauls have been seized at the Port City of

noteworthy. The two were extradited to
the U.S. for trial, where they pleaded guilty
to, among other crimes, trafficking heroin
and methamphetamine.

struggling to survive in Nairobi,
despite his lifestyle in the affluent
leafy suburban neighbourhood
dotted with bistros, grills and
bars.
However, a closer look at MBA's
financials revealed a man of means. He
funded the field operations at the Namanga
site by sending loads of cash to Betty.
Moreover, MBA also owned a company
(Ngara Associate Investment Company)
and a fleet of transport trucks back in
Nigeria. He was also listed as a director in
a local Kenyan company.
Upon thorough interrogation, detectives
established that MBA's kin, Agwu
Ojukwu (alias Deacon or Pastor), was the
mastermind and architect of the entire
clandestine lab. They also learned that
MBA had just jetted into the country
on October 2 to assess the progress in
Namanga.
The DCI placed a stop order against
Ojukwu at Jomo Kenyatta International
Airport (JKIA), right on cue, to arrest him
on October 3 before he fled the country.
The culprit hardly left the airport when
word got to him that his associates in the
Namanga business were in police custody.
He attempted to book the next available
flight out of the country and escape the
hostile ground. Unfortunately for him, it
was too late.
On searching Ojukwu's luggage, police
discovered crucial pieces of evidence,
including the original land sale agreement
for the ranch in Namanga where the
temporary lab structures were erected.
The land sale agreement bore the name
of Ojukwu's alleged Kenyan wife as the
buyer. Also seized were copies of the
site's construction plan, a list of fencing
materials, a copy of the land title deed
from which the land was to be excised and
a handset.
Further investigations revealed Ojukwu
to be a multinational businessman who
visited Kenya for the first time in 2007,
allegedly for undisclosed business. Besides
owning multiple businesses in Nigeria,
Gabon, South Africa and China, he is also
linked to a drug cartel in South America.
He is also believed to be a gold smuggler
across the continent and beyond.
As investigations intensified, fingers
pointed to a fourth suspect, 41-year-old
Alvarado Israel Vera, a former member
of the Mexican Police's investigative unit.
Alvarado had arrived in the country
months earlier, alongside two other
compatriots, Carlos Pedro and Ignacio
Morales Alvarez. A stop order was also
placed against him and his crew at the
JKIA. He was arrested on October 5
during a botched attempt to escape back to
Mexico. His crew holed up.
Deeper inquiries into the case established
that Ojukwu had contracted the three
Mexicans for their expertise in 'cooking'
synthetic opioid (Methamphetamine). The
three Mexicans had spent several days at
the Namanga lab setting up the equipment
and receiving chemicals, as they were
tasked with guiding the facility's full
operationalisation.
On October 9, 2024, the police arrested
Caroline Wambui Muchira, 52, a
businesswoman, for her involvement in
coordinating with Ojukwu during the
purchase of the chemicals. A month later,
a sixth suspect, Francis Maina Gachau,
was also arrested in Juja. Maina was a
middleman involved in the distribution of

The discovery informed the police's

The chemicals highlighted above are

OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
For Immediate Release
PRESS STATEMENT
National Police Service Headquarters, Nairobi
UPDATE ON CASES OF ABDUCTIONS IN THE COUNTRY
Following the recent reported cases of suspected abductions of persons in the
country, the National Police Service wishes to update the public on four cases
reported in December 2024 as follows;
Bernard Kavuli Musyimi who was reported missing at Ngong' Police Station
presented himself at Moi's Bridge Police Station today and is assisting the
investigators with further information.
Following media reports that Billy Wanyiri Mwangi, Peter Muteti and Rony
Kiplagat who were reported missing in Embu Police Station, Kabete Police
Station and Thogoto Police Post respectively have re-united with their respective
families, we wish to assure the public that our officer will reach out to them and
their families and give them all the necessary support as we seek further
information to assist ongoing investigations.
Notably, the Directorate of Criminal Investigations is investigating all cases of
missing persons in the country with most of the cases currently pending before
court and others under active investigations.
We therefore wish to appeal to members of the public to collaborate with us, by
providing any information that may aid in investigations or tracing their
whereabouts. All information is helpful and can be reported to the nearest police
station or our toll-free lines 999, 911, 112 or FichuakwaDCI 0800722203.
The National Police Service remains committed to ensuring that all these matters
are thoroughly investigated to their logical conclusions.
DR. RESILA ONYANGO, PhD, HSC
For: INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
January 6, 2025
Encls.

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
PRESS STATEMENT
STATEMENT ON THE SHOOTING OF LAWYER KYALO MBOBU
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) commiserates with the family,
friends and associates of Lawyer Kyalo Mbobu who was shot in a drive by shooting
incident that took place on 9th September, 2025 along Magadi road.
We wish to inform the public that immediately the incident was reported, the scene
was visited by a team of detectives under the leadership of RCIO Nairobi. After
securing the scene, detectives from the DCI Homicide Bureau supported by experts
from the National Forensic Laboratory carefully examined the scene and collected
critical evidence essential to the investigations.
The DCI is committed to ensuring that the perpetrators of this heinous act are
brought to justice. Our investigators are working diligently, employing all available
resources and expertise to piece together the events surrounding this incident.
We appeal for calm during this challenging time and request the public's cooperation
as we work to resolve this case. We are determined to provide the justice that Lawyer
Kyalo Mbobu and his loved ones deserve.
We further appeal to anyone with information that could assist the investigations to
report to the nearest police station, #FichuaKwaDCI toll free number 0800 722 203
or forward the information confidentially to the DCI through Whatsapp number
0709 570 000.
More information regarding the on-going investigations will be released to the public
at an appropriate time.
John Marete, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
September 10, 2025

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) commiserates with the family,
friends and associates of Lawyer Kyalo Mbobu who was shot in a drive by shooting
incident that took place on 9th September, 2025 along Magadi road.
We wish to inform the public that immediately the incident was reported, the scene
was visited by a team of detectives under the leadership of RCIO Nairobi. After
securing the scene, detectives from the DCI Homicide Bureau supported by experts
from the National Forensic Laboratory carefully examined the scene and collected
critical evidence essential to the investigations.
The DCI is committed to ensuring that the perpetrators of this heinous act are
brought to justice. Our investigators are working diligently, employing all available
resources and expertise to piece together the events surrounding this incident.
We appeal for calm during this challenging time and request the public's cooperation
as we work to resolve this case. We are determined to provide the justice that Lawyer
Kyalo Mbobu and his loved ones deserve.
We further appeal to anyone with information that could assist the investigations to
report to the nearest police station, #FichuaKwaDCI toll free number 0800 722 203
or forward the information confidentially to the DCI through Whatsapp number
0709 570 000.
More information regarding the on-going investigations will be released to the public
at an appropriate time.
John Marete, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
September 10, 2025

ALLEGATIONS OF ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCES AND TORTURE
The National Police Service (NPS) has noted allegations circulating in
mainstream and social media regarding enforced disappearances and
torture.
As a Service committed to accountability and transparency, we take
these claims seriously. We therefore urge anyone with information or
specific allegations of enforced disappearance, torture, or other
human rights violations to report the matter immediately at the
nearest police station.
Furthermore, we acknowledge receipt of a report of a missing person,
namely Davis Lichuma, which was made at Central Police Station in
Nairobi.
We guarantee that all reports will be investigated thoroughly,
professionally, impartially, and expeditiously, in accordance with the
law.
The National Police Service remains fully dedicated to professional
policing that serves and protects all Kenyans, residents, and visitors.
We uphold the constitutional rights of every person and strictly follow
all legal procedures in our operations.
We remain steadfast in our commitment to the highest standards of
professionalism, respect for human rights, and full adherence to the
Constitution of Kenya and all other relevant laws.
MUCH RI NYAGA

NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
June 28, 2026

PRESS STATEMENT
MAZINGIRA HOUSE
KIAMBU ROAD
P.O. Box 30036
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
UPDATE ON THE INVESTIGATIONS OF FRAUDULENT AND NON-COMPLIANT FILES FROM SHA
AND KMPDC
On September 1, 2025, the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) received 1,188 files from the
Social Health Authority (SHA) and the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council (KMPDC).
The files pertain to individuals, organisations, and various parties believed to be involved in
healthcare fraud, thereby undermining government initiatives to provide quality healthcare services
to the public.
Thorough and expedient investigations were immediately initiated upon receipt of the files. A multi-
agency team, led by the DCI, was formed to conduct a comprehensive review of the materials. The
aim is to ensure that all individuals involved in any form of healthcare fraud are held accountable for
their actions.
We wish to inform the general public that the 1,188 files are at various stages of investigation.
Currently, five suspects are in custody pending arraignment on Monday, October 6, 2025. Efforts to
apprehend additional suspects are already underway, following approval from the ODPP. The
suspects will be arraigned on various charges, including offences under the Penal Code, the Proceeds
of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Act, the Social Health Insurance Act, and the Anti-Corruption
and Economic Crimes Act.
The DCI remains resolute in its commitment to stopping healthcare fraud, holding all offenders
accountable, and, in collaboration with other law enforcement agencies, ensuring that all assets and
resources acquired fraudulently are recovered. The public will be kept informed on the progress of
the investigations through regular updates.
Together, let's safeguard the integrity of our healthcare system and ensure that quality services are
delivered to all citizens by reporting any suspicious activities to the DCI via the #FichuaKwaDCI toll-
free number 0800 722 203 or via WhatsApp on 0709 570 000.
John Marete, HSC

text:
The DCI
Land Fraud
ARDHIPHOUSE
LAND FRAUD Still a Menace
but Police Are Top of the Game
By Jonah Kimani
'n October 2024, two Nairobi city
traders Jacob Mwangi Mungai and
Patrick Magu Kamau - were charged at
the Milimani law courts with conspiracy to
defraud a businessman of his parcel of land
worth Sh 230 million. The two were also
accused of forgery.
According to the charges, the duo,
alongside others not before the court,
had in 2010 forged a letter of allotment
for a 3.2-acre piece of land, intending
to commit fraud. Documents obtained
from the Lands Registry showed that the
land in dispute was registered under the
Bahati Development Welfare Association.
Mwangi and Magu were released on a KES
one million bond. The case is anything but
unique. On the contrary, land fraud cases
continue to rock Nairobi and other major
towns in the country.
Such cases include reports of real estate
businesses and landowners clashing after
landowners with undeveloped plots wake
up to skyscraper buildings erected on their
property. The property development is
typically the work of document bearers,
who are either victims of fraud or
perpetrators linked to daring land cartels.
Land cartels often target underdeveloped
parcels of land, especially those owned
by persons deemed not powerful or well-
connected in society, including elderly
couples or poor families. They operate
by invading the underdeveloped land,
bringing down whatever structures are
erected on the land, and commencing
construction, notwithstanding that
they lack the documentation to carry
out such endeavours. Additionally, they
often collude with rogue officials in law
enforcement and government ministries,
and this unholy alliance makes the pursuit
of justice take ages. Worst case scenario,
the downtrodden may never receive
justice, or the daunting court battle may be
the end of them.
However, there may be one ray of hope
for land fraud victims: land fraud is one
crime the DCI is committed to curtailing.
The Directorate often deploys teams
to conduct operations that target land
grabbers, the counterfeiters who forge the
documents handed to unsuspecting buyers
of fraudulently acquired properties, and
other perpetrators within the elaborate
land fraud scam.
15
In one recent crackdown conducted on
March 28, 2025, eight suspects found
forging land ownership documents and
other government-related documents with
the intent to defraud innocent members
of the public were arrested and charged.
The operation followed a tip-off from a
concerned citizen.
During the coordinated operations,
Livingstone Ambai Munala, Dan Adero.
Okoth, Nicholas Mukuna Ayela, Paul
Muigai Kimani, Kennedy Mulatya, Patrice
Matheka
Josaya Tumbo, Emmanuel
Mutuku, and Leonard Clifford Wafula
were all arrested in separate raids.
Detectives discovered multiple assorted
land documents belonging to different
individuals, including: dozens of plain and
original title deeds, 287 assorted stamps,
blank grant titles and allotment letters,
15
---
Jacob Mwangi Mungai and Patrick Kamau when they appeared at Millimani law Courts over
conspiracy to defraud land worth over Sh 230 million.
11 unused green cards, 101 passport-size photos for different individuals,
certificates of title, numerous transfer documents among other evidential
materials during the series of arrests.
Notably, Dan Okoth was an assistant security officer at the Ministry of Lands
Survey of Kenya, Emanuel Matheka a casual labourer at Ardhi House -
Nairobi, Josaya Tumbo a land broker, while Clifford Wafula worked at the
Government Press as a Printer II. The suspects were arraigned at Milimani
Law Courts, and their case is ongoing.
The head of the Land Fraud Investigative Unit pointed out that the arrest
came at a time when the land fraud menace had rocked the Capital owing to
the lucrative real estate business.
Suspected Serial Scammer Back in Custody for Land Fraud
A few months earlier (December 2024), detectives from the Operations
Directorate had once again arrested a suspected serial fraudster, Brian
Otiende Ayanga. Ayanga is the supposed ring leader of a city cartel that had
become the nightmare of land owners and developers around the Capital.
The cartel was notorious for issuing fake title deeds while purporting to work
at the Nairobi County Lands Registry.
Ayanga's arrest came barely two weeks after his accomplice, Lawrence
Martins Ochieng, was arrested for his involvement in a land fraud case
where a victim almost lost two prime parcels of land located in Nairobi's
Pumwani area. According to the victim, Brian's gang had issued him with
fake documents purporting to be genuine certificates of lease. Although the
fraud was intercepted, the victim lost over KES 553,000 to the machinations.
On learning that Ochieng was in the custody of the
DCI's Operations Support Unit detectives, Ayanga
went into hiding along Katulo Road in Buruburu.
However, a relentless two-week manhunt saw him
swept from the warmth of his couch and taken into
custody. With another gold scam case still pending in
the courts, Angaya continues to fight for an assurance
of liberty.
As more and more victims thronged police stations
with related complaints, the DCI cautions
landowners, especially those in upscale suburbs, of the
organized criminal ring that is targeting their parcels
of land to obtain hefty sums of money using forged
documents. To lower the risk of early detection and
go whole hog with their fraudulence, the cartel's main
target is the landowners entering into joint ventures
with developers.
The criminal enterprise set in at a time when developers
were approaching individuals with underdeveloped
plots and enticing them with profitable terms for the
development of the land. More often than not, the
agreement would require the landowner to obtain
certificates of lease, which had then become the soft
spot for the fraudsters.
For instance, in the incident highlighted above,
where a victim lost money over land in Pumwani, the
victim could have lost his two parcels of land had a
keen developer not sought the services of a thorough
city advocate. Nonetheless, he lost KES 553,550 to
the cartel that posed as staff at the Nairobi County
Lands Registry. Martin Ochieng, Ayanga's accomplice,
had approached the victim and promised to get him
certificates of lease for both parcels of land.
Notably, most of the suspects implicated in the case
were renowned gold scammers who had taken a break
from that field and were testing the waters in the land
fraud venture. Luckily, they're on the DCI Operations
team's radar, and the Directorate continues hunting
them down one after the other.

to conduct operations that target land
grabbers, the counterfeiters who forge the
documents handed to unsuspecting buyers
of fraudulently acquired properties, and
other perpetrators within the elaborate
land fraud scam.
15
In one recent crackdown conducted on
March 28, 2025, eight suspects found
forging land ownership documents and
other government-related documents with
the intent to defraud innocent members
of the public were arrested and charged.
The operation followed a tip-off from a
concerned citizen.
During the coordinated operations,
Livingstone Ambai Munala, Dan Adero.
Okoth, Nicholas Mukuna Ayela, Paul
Muigai Kimani, Kennedy Mulatya, Patrice
Matheka
Josaya Tumbo, Emmanuel
Mutuku, and Leonard Clifford Wafula
were all arrested in separate raids.
Detectives discovered multiple assorted
land documents belonging to different
individuals, including: dozens of plain and
original title deeds, 287 assorted stamps,
blank grant titles and allotment letters,
15
---
Jacob Mwangi Mungai and Patrick Kamau when they appeared at Millimani law Courts over
conspiracy to defraud land worth over Sh 230 million.
11 unused green cards, 101 passport-size photos for different individuals,
certificates of title, numerous transfer documents among other evidential
materials during the series of arrests.
Notably, Dan Okoth was an assistant security officer at the Ministry of Lands
Survey of Kenya, Emanuel Matheka a casual labourer at Ardhi House -
Nairobi, Josaya Tumbo a land broker, while Clifford Wafula worked at the
Government Press as a Printer II. The suspects were arraigned at Milimani
Law Courts, and their case is ongoing.
The head of the Land Fraud Investigative Unit pointed out that the arrest
came at a time when the land fraud menace had rocked the Capital owing to
the lucrative real estate business.
Suspected Serial Scammer Back in Custody for Land Fraud
A few months earlier (December 2024), detectives from the Operations
Directorate had once again arrested a suspected serial fraudster, Brian
Otiende Ayanga. Ayanga is the supposed ring leader of a city cartel that had
become the nightmare of land owners and developers around the Capital.
The cartel was notorious for issuing fake title deeds while purporting to work
at the Nairobi County Lands Registry.
Ayanga's arrest came barely two weeks after his accomplice, Lawrence
Martins Ochieng, was arrested for his involvement in a land fraud case
where a victim almost lost two prime parcels of land located in Nairobi's
Pumwani area. According to the victim, Brian's gang had issued him with
fake documents purporting to be genuine certificates of lease. Although the
fraud was intercepted, the victim lost over KES 553,000 to the machinations.
On learning that Ochieng was in the custody of the
DCI's Operations Support Unit detectives, Ayanga
went into hiding along Katulo Road in Buruburu.
However, a relentless two-week manhunt saw him
swept from the warmth of his couch and taken into
custody. With another gold scam case still pending in
the courts, Angaya continues to fight for an assurance
of liberty.
As more and more victims thronged police stations
with related complaints, the DCI cautions
landowners, especially those in upscale suburbs, of the
organized criminal ring that is targeting their parcels
of land to obtain hefty sums of money using forged
documents. To lower the risk of early detection and
go whole hog with their fraudulence, the cartel's main
target is the landowners entering into joint ventures
with developers.
The criminal enterprise set in at a time when developers
were approaching individuals with underdeveloped
plots and enticing them with profitable terms for the
development of the land. More often than not, the
agreement would require the landowner to obtain
certificates of lease, which had then become the soft
spot for the fraudsters.
For instance, in the incident highlighted above,
where a victim lost money over land in Pumwani, the
victim could have lost his two parcels of land had a
keen developer not sought the services of a thorough
city advocate. Nonetheless, he lost KES 553,550 to
the cartel that posed as staff at the Nairobi County
Lands Registry. Martin Ochieng, Ayanga's accomplice,
had approached the victim and promised to get him
certificates of lease for both parcels of land.
Notably, most of the suspects implicated in the case
were renowned gold scammers who had taken a break
from that field and were testing the waters in the land
fraud venture. Luckily, they're on the DCI Operations
team's radar, and the Directorate continues hunting
them down one after the other.

PRESS RELEASE
UPDATE ON THE ONGOING INVESTIGATION INTO THE MURDER OF PCEA CLERIC
IN NAKURU
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) wishes to provide the public with an
update on the ongoing investigation into the murder of Reverend Julius Ndumia Ngari,
which occurred on the night of Sunday, May 3, 2026, at PCEA Tabuga Church in
Nakuru North Sub-County.
Through sustained forensic and intelligence-driven investigations, detectives have
firmly linked the incident to a notorious criminal gang first profiled in July 2022. The
gang is known for carrying out violent armed robberies using an L1A1 firearm while
disguised in security forces attire. The firearm in question was recovered by police in
2024.
The same gang has also been connected to a violent robbery on the night of May 1,
2026, during which Sh600,000 was transferred from a victim's bank account to
mobile numbers associated with the group.
Detectives are also investigating a pattern of violent attacks and robberies within
Nakuru County and its environs. It is suspected that the same gang is behind several of
these incidents.
Advanced forensic examinations, including scientific analysis aimed at placing the
suspects at the crime scene, are still ongoing to build a robust case for prosecution.
Further updates will be provided as the investigation progresses.
The DCI reaffirms its commitment to a thorough, professional, and impartial
investigation to ensure all those involved in this heinous crime are brought to justice.
We urge members of the public to remain calm, avoid speculation, and continue
cooperating with investigators by providing any relevant information.
---
Anyone with information that may aid the investigation is urged to report to the nearest
police station or anonymously through the #FichuaKwaDCI hotline by calling 0800
722 203 (Toll-free) or via WhatsApp on 0709 570 000.
John Marete, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
May 12, 2026

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
PRESS STATEMENT
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
STATEMENT ON THE RECEIPT OF 1,188 FRAUDULENT AND NON-COMPLIANT FILES
FROM SHA AND KMPDC
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) wishes to inform the public that it
has today received 1,188 files from Social Health Authority (SHA) and the Kenya
Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council (KMPDC). The files pertain to individuals,
entities and various parties suspected of engaging in health care fraud thereby
undermining the government efforts aimed at delivering quality healthcare services
to the citizenry.
Upon receipt of the files, a multi-agency team has been constituted under the
leadership of the DCI with a view of expeditiously reviewing the files. The objective of
this review is to make sure that all those who have been involved in any form of
healthcare fraud will be arraigned regardless of their social status and political
affiliations.
In collaboration with all other law enforcement agencies, the DCI is committed to
recovering all assets and other resources acquired through fraudulent means. The
public will be kept informed on the progress of the investigations through regular
updates.
The DCI remains at the forefront in supporting all government and non-
governmental entities in the fight against all forms of fraud, while urging the public
to remain vigilant and report such criminalities via the #FichuaKwaDCI toll-free
number 0800 722 203 or WhatsApp on 0709 570 000.
John Marete, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
September 1, 2025
