text:
The DCI
Blood on Ancestral Soil
SIO-PORT POLICE STATION
Blood on Ancestral Soil
Two Dailed Over Fatal
Land Dispute
By: Elijah Gakuya
t was 6:00 a.m., a chilly morning
in the lush green fields of Funyula,
overlooking the majestic Samia
Hills. The golden sun's rays struggled to
penetrate the dense, imposing trees as
Patrick Wandera Oduori arose from the
warmth of his dreams. Unbeknownst
to him, this would be the final time he
would wake up on this side of eternity.
Wandera, who had lived with his family
in Mombasa for many years, had arrived
in Segero B Village, Funyula, with his
wife and children just a day before.
Working through his productive years
before finally retiring to his ancestral
26
DECEMBER | 2025
village was Wandera's lifelong plan. His
brothers welcomed them with open
arms after their long absence. Ready to
start his retirement life, Wandera had
his breakfast, a hot cup of tea, grabbed a
jembe, and walked into a small portion
of land located just next to his house
with his wife, Maculate Akinyi Wandera,
in tow. The piece in question had been
hived off from a larger parcel belonging
to his late grandfather and preserved for
his return. Soon after, three women he'd
hired to help them till the land joined
him and Maculate to begin the day's
work. Ten minutes into their work,
three shadowy figures appeared through
the morning mist. Wandera, who had
only hired three workers, turned to the
three women and asked, "You didn't
invite other friends, did you?" "No, not
at all," one rejoined.
Before they could identify the strangers,
Joseph Ongoro Wanjala emerged from
the mist like a ghost of vengeance, his
two sons flanking him in a menacing
arrowhead formation, ready for
any eventuality. Ongoro wielded a
machete in his right hand, with the
left supporting the three hoes slung
over his shoulder. The trio halted just
three meters shy of Wandera's position,
26/88
---
The DCI
Blood on Ancestral Soil
Detective Kelvin Munywoki of DCI Samia at the scene of the murder, recounts what
transpired on the fateful day. PHOTO/ELIJAH GAKUYA
Ongoro's fury visible in the veins bulging
on his forehead. Ongoro's reputation as
the village troublemaker preceded him.
So, his presence spelt trouble. After
a minute of tense silence, he began
hurling accusations, claiming Wandera
was tilling his land. Wandera's attempts
to explain that this was his grandfather's
portion only fueled Ongoro's anger.
Ongoro, whose rage was now at its
boiling point, ordered Wandera and his
wife to vacate the land, promising dire
consequences if they refused.
Certain of his claim, Wandera stood his
ground. He resolved to defend his land
or die trying. Unfortunately for him,
Ongoro was not one to take no for an
answer. He handed the machete to his
son, Kevin Ongoro, and ordered him
to strike. Kevin, without hesitation,
advanced towards Wandera with the
machete firmly gripped. One swing was
all it took to inflict a severe injury to
Wandera's head, narrowly missing his
right ear. Everything fell silent.
Maculate could not believe her eyes;
neither could the hired women. It was
a scene straight out of a horror film. As
Wandera collapsed to the ground, the
grim reality of what had just happened
began to sink in. Maculate let out a
wail loud enough to reach Wandera's
two brothers, Obiji and Akala. Obiji,
who was inside his house, dropped
everything and dashed towards the
source of the scream, while Akala, who
was heading to work, changed course
and rushed to the scene.
By then, Kevin and his brother, Semi,
had begun kicking the women in
an attempt to drive them away. The
commotion drew the attention of a few
neighbors, who arrived to find chaos.
In the melee, Ongoro and his sons
vanished like tears in the rain. The
trio later reappeared at Funyula Police
Station, where they filed separate false
reports claiming Wandera and his family
had assaulted them. Fighting back tears,
Obiji and Akala carried their brother
to a nearby road where they found a
motorcycle. Akala helped the injured
Wandera onto the bike and sped toward
Funyula Police Station, with Maculate
and Obiji following closely.
At the station, the police officers
manning the report office desk were
shocked by the gory sight. They urged
the family to seek immediate medical
help to stop the excessive bleeding.
Heeding the advice, they rushed to the
nearest facility, Nangina Holy Family
Hospital. Although the hospital's
staff performed scans, the under-
equipped hospital could not provide the
specialized care Wandera needed.
Moreover, the victim had lost
consciousness owing to the shock from
the blood loss. Therefore, the hospital
staff referred him to Busia County
Referral Hospital. Wandera's brothers
and wife immediately set off for Busia,
Entrance to Nangina Holy Family Hospital where the victim was first rushed to after the
incident PHOTO/ELIJAH GAKUYA
DECEMBER | 2025
27
88
---
The DCI
BB
Blood on Ancestral Soil
Funyula Police Station where initial investigations
were carried out before they were handed over to
DCI Samia. PHOTO/ELIJAH GAKUYA
only to find the hospital deserted-a
doctors' strike had paralyzed the
facility for days now. The discovery was
devastating, given that Busia County
Referral Hospital was the only Referral
facility in the area. Back to square one,
they scrambled to find another facility in
Busia town, Wandera's life now dangling
by a thread.
A quick-thinking Akala suggested they
rush Wandera to New Busia Nursing and
Maternity Hospital, which admitted him
as an emergency case. He underwent
an immediate CT scan, which revealed
that the force with which Kevin had
struck him fractured his skull, causing
blood to seep into his brain. Therefore,
an emergency surgery was necessary.
After hours in the operating room,
Wandera's will to live had conquered
death. His regaining consciousness was
a relief for Maculate and her brothers-
in-law, who had kept vigil. Moreover,
his condition improved so much that he
could recognize and speak to visitors. In
a brief chat with his wife, he lamented,
"Ongoro wanted to kill me, yet I hadn't
even stayed on the land for long." For a
few days, he remained stable-until he
wasn't.
Fifteen days after the operation,
his health deteriorated rapidly.
Another emergency surgery had to
be performed, fast. Unfortunately, his
condition remained bleak. With options
exhausted, the hospital referred the
family to Moi Teaching and Referral
Hospital in Eldoret for specialized care.
28
DECEMBER | 2025
For the family, the trip to Eldoret meant
breaking the bank. So, they began
fundraising for transport.
As fate would have it, Wandera breathed
his last before the funds were secured.
The news was devastating. It was a day
of profound grief for Maculate and
Wandera's brothers, who struggled to
comprehend life's fragility. While his
body was moved to Francis Funeral
Home for a post-mortem examination,
Maculate's sorrow hardened into a
focused anger; anger that she would
train towards those who had deeply
wounded her husband, and now her life.
In her deepest thoughts, she vowed
vengeance, albeit through legal means.
The wheels of justice began turning as
soon as she reported the death to the
police.
Upon receiving the news, the Officer
Commanding Funyula Police Station
(OCS) knew where to start. He
dispatched his officers to Segero B
Village, where they found Ongoro
and his son, Semi, relaxing in their
homesteads after a long day of causing
mayhem, and quickly handcuffed them.
Although Kevin, the main perpetrator,
was not in the homestead during the
arrest, his freedom was temporary. Once
at the police station, Ongoro called his
son. Surprisingly, Kevin walked in and
surrendered. All perpetrators were now
in custody, awaiting arraignment in
court.
The OCS Funyula Police Station passed
the case to the Directorate of Criminal
Investigations (DCI), Samia, for
intensive investigation. The first stop was
the land, which was now both the crime
scene and the motive. Investigations
confirmed the plot rightfully belonged
to Wandera. The two men's pieces of
land shared a border; Ongoro had
encroached onto Wandera's side, yet
seeing Wandera till the disputed area
provoked his fatal reaction.
With motive established and eyewitness
accounts recorded, the case began at
the Busia High Court. For nearly two
years, DCI detectives and prosecutors
meticulously presented evidence to
secure convictions.
Their efforts bore fruit. After evaluating
the evidence, Busia High Court Judge
W.M. Musyoka sentenced Joseph
Ongoro to 30 years in prison. Kevin
Ongoro, who wielded the machete,
received 25 years. Semi, who played no
direct part in the murder, was acquitted.
The sentence brought a measure of
solace to Wandera's family. Justice, at
last, had been served.
Wandera's family struggles to fill the
void left by a loving husband, father,
and brother. Despite their grief, they
can only hope that dialogue will replace
the senseless murders caused by land
disputes. Through dialogue, families
can avoid losing their sons to graves and
prisons.
Busia Law Courts where the two accused persons were
handed sentences. PHOTO/ELIJAH GAKUYA
I hereby sentence
the 1st accused to 25
years imprisonment,
and the 2nd
accused to 30 years
imprisonment. There
is a right of appeal,
of 14 days, from the
date hereof
Busia High Court
Judge W.M. Musyoka
28/88

The wheels of justice began turning as
soon as she reported the death to the
police.
Upon receiving the news, the Officer
Commanding Funyula Police Station
(OCS) knew where to start. He
dispatched his officers to Segero B
Village, where they found Ongoro
and his son, Semi, relaxing in their
homesteads after a long day of causing
mayhem, and quickly handcuffed them.
Although Kevin, the main perpetrator,
was not in the homestead during the
arrest, his freedom was temporary. Once
at the police station, Ongoro called his
son. Surprisingly, Kevin walked in and
surrendered. All perpetrators were now
in custody, awaiting arraignment in
court.
The OCS Funyula Police Station passed
the case to the Directorate of Criminal
Investigations (DCI), Samia, for
intensive investigation. The first stop was
the land, which was now both the crime
scene and the motive. Investigations
confirmed the plot rightfully belonged
to Wandera. The two men's pieces of
land shared a border; Ongoro had
encroached onto Wandera's side, yet
seeing Wandera till the disputed area
provoked his fatal reaction.
With motive established and eyewitness
accounts recorded, the case began at
the Busia High Court. For nearly two
years, DCI detectives and prosecutors
meticulously presented evidence to
secure convictions.
Their efforts bore fruit. After evaluating
the evidence, Busia High Court Judge
W.M. Musyoka sentenced Joseph
Ongoro to 30 years in prison. Kevin
Ongoro, who wielded the machete,
received 25 years. Semi, who played no
direct part in the murder, was acquitted.
The sentence brought a measure of
solace to Wandera's family. Justice, at
last, had been served.
Wandera's family struggles to fill the
void left by a loving husband, father,
and brother. Despite their grief, they
can only hope that dialogue will replace
the senseless murders caused by land
disputes. Through dialogue, families
can avoid losing their sons to graves and
prisons.
Busia Law Courts where the two accused persons were
handed sentences. PHOTO/ELIJAH GAKUYA

years imprisonment,
and the 2nd
accused to 30 years
imprisonment. There
is a right of appeal,
of 14 days, from the

OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS STATEMENT
National Police Service Headquarters
For Immediate Release
RESURFACING OF ONE NDIANGUI KINYAGIA
The National Police Service (NPS) has noted the resurfacing of one Ndiangui
Kinyagia from his hideout and subsequent appearance in court today, 3rd July
2025.
Ndiangui Kinyagia had been reported missing, and information circulating on
social as well as mainstream media accused the Police Service of allegedly
abducting him. Nonetheless, he remains a person of interest to the police and
is hereby urged to present himself to the DCI Headquarters to record a
statement.
The Service reiterates its earlier response that Ndiangui Kinyagia was not in
police custody. We take great exception to the emerging trend whereby
individuals feign abduction and provide false information to the police,
intending to generate a misleading narrative that exploits public outrage and
sensational headlines, thereby distorting the truth rather than focusing on
justice.
These criminal acts undermine the integrity of our law enforcement
efforts, damage the reputation of the National Police Service, and cause
anxiety to the public.
The National Police Service wishes to remind the public that stage-managed
abductions and providing false information to the police are criminal offences
punishable by law. We therefore warn all persons against engaging in such
acts.
NPS reaffirms its commitment to upholding the highest standards of fidelity
to the Constitution, operational independence, impartiality, and political
neutrality in fulfilling its role of maintaining law and order.
MUCH RI NYAGA
DIRECTOR CORPORATE COMMUNICATION/SPOKESPERSON
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
July 03, 2025

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
PRESS STATEMENT
CLARIFICATION/FACTS FOLLOWING ARREST OF SEVEN FRAUD SUSPECTS AT
HARAMBEE HOUSE
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) wishes to set the record straight and
strongly refute misleading and sensationalized headlines and reports appearing in
sections of the media, particularly The Standard, concerning the arrest of seven
individuals at Harambee House on 10th March, 2026.
Key facts of the matter are as follows:
On 10th March, 2026, DCI detectives, acting on credible intelligence, arrested seven
suspects who had illegally accessed a boardroom on the 12th floor of Harambee
House. The suspects were masquerading as officials from the Ministry of Interior,
National Treasury, Ministry of Health and had lured two foreign nationals - Mr.
Talal Yousef Yousef Zaitoun, representing M/S Jokara AB (a Swedish company), and
his brother Mr. Hatem Youssef Yousef Zaitoun ― into a fictitious government tender
for the supply of 500 Toyota Hiace High Roof Ambulances.
The detectives had earlier established that the fraudulent scheme commenced on 10th
January, 2026 when Mr. Talal Zaitoun received an unsolicited WhatsApp message
from an individual by the name Stanley Ndawula who requested the company
catalogue and later connected him to Geoffrey Were, who presented himself as a
consultant with Interlog Corporate, supposedly working with government entities.
On 26th January, 2026, the victim travelled to Kenya, was received at the airport by
the said Geoffrey Were and a driver, and taken to Harambee House. A female
accomplice facilitated illegal entry past security checkpoints. The victim was taken to
a conference room located on the 5th floor and was introduced to individuals posing
as representatives of Treasury and the Ministry of Health. He was presented with
forged tender documents, including a fake pre-qualification certificate purportedly
signed by the Head of Procurement and the Principal Secretary, Ministry of Interior.
The fraudsters offered two packages: USD 90,000 for a single five-year business
opportunity or USD 110,000 for multiple opportunities over the same period. The
victim opted for the higher package and transferred USD 110,000 on 30th January
2026, from a sister company in China to Conrad Law Advocates LLP Account
domiciled at Ecobank Kenya.
---
On 11th February 2026, an additional USD 360,750 was transferred to the same
account under the pretext of insurance, bringing total funds fraudulently obtained
totaling to USD 470,750. At the time of arrest, the fraudsters were pressing for a
further USD 1,080,000 in installments, prompting the victims to return to Kenya for
further negotiations. Upon arrival, they were again taken to a 12th-floor boardroom
where they met suspects who were later arrested.
The suspects arrested were Geoffrey Were Odondi, Michael Musyoki Ngumbi,
Kororia Simatwa, Evans Simotwo, Allan Muthaiga Kariuki and Munialo Jared
Masinde who were found not to be government employees. The seventh suspect,
Purity Njeri Njiami was found to have been a former employee of the Ministry of
Public Service who was transferred to the Treasury eight years ago. Purity is the
individual who illegally facilitated access to the boardrooms but held no current
position at Harambee House or the Ministry of Interior.
On 16th March 2026, all seven suspects were arraigned before the Milimani Law
Courts and charged with: Conspiracy to defraud contrary to Section 317 of the Penal
Code, Obtaining money by false pretenses contrary to Section 313 of the Penal Code,
Acquisition of proceeds of crime contrary to Section 4(a) as read with Section 16(1)
of the Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2009 and Forgery
contrary to Section 345 as read with Section 349 of the Penal Code.
They pleaded not guilty and were released on bond of KSh 5 million each or cash bail
of KSh 300,000 with two sureties. All their passports were surrendered to court. The
matter is set for mention on 1st April, 2026 for pre-trial directions.
The DCI wishes to emphasize that no serving government official or employee of the
Ministry of Interior was involved in this criminal enterprise. The arrested persons
were purely external fraudsters who exploited public institutions for criminal gain.
The successful arrest underscores the effectiveness of inter-agency collaboration and
the vigilance of genuine public servants who assisted in exposing the syndicate.
Further, members of the public and international investors are reminded that all
legitimate government tenders are advertised through official channels and no
genuine government tender requires upfront facilitation fees, insurance, commitment
deposits, or payments to private law firms or personal accounts. Any person
demanding such payments is almost certainly a fraudster.
The DCI remains committed to dismantling organized fraud syndicates targeting both
local and foreign investors and will work with other government agencies while
pursuing all available legal avenues to recover the stolen funds and secure
convictions.
JOHN MARETE, HSC
FOR DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
March 20, 2026

text:
NATIONAL
POLICE
SERVICE
DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
WANTED SUSPECT
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) is appealing to members of the public to
provide any information that may assist in the arrest of Ben Shapaya, who is wanted pursuant
to a warrant of arrest issued by the Kibera Chief Magistrates' Court in Criminal Case No.
E599/2025.
Shapaya, a resident of Isanjiro Village, Musingu Location, Kakamega County, was arraigned
before the court on June 10, 2025, and charged with the offence of Cheating contrary to
Section 315 of the Penal Code. He subsequently failed to appear before the court, prompting
the issuance of a warrant of arrest.
The suspect is reported to have posed as a medical doctor based in Mombasa and obtained
money from several unsuspecting individuals by falsely claiming that he could facilitate the
importation of motor vehicles from Japan on their behalf. He is accused of subsequently
defrauding the victims of their hard-earned money.
The DCI is therefore urging anyone who may have information regarding Shapaya's
whereabouts to come forward and assist in bringing him to justice.
If you know his whereabouts, #Fichua KwaDCI through the DCI toll-free hotline 0800 722 203
or WhatsApp number 0709 570 000. Information may also be reported at the nearest police
station or through the national police emergency hotlines 999, 911 or 112.
Every piece of information matters. Your information could help bring a wanted person to
justice.
Ben Shapaya

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
FURTHER UPDATE ON INVESTIGATIONS INTO FIRE INCIDENT AT UTUMISHI
GIRLS SENIOR SECONDARY SCHOOL IN GILGIL
Following the on-going in-depth investigation into the tragic fire incident that
occurred on Thursday, May 28, 2026, at Utumishi Girls Senior Secondary School
in Gilgil, Nakuru County, in which sixteen students lost their lives, the
Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) has achieved significant progress
and a major breakthrough has been achieved. After conducting a through
detailed forensic analysis of the CCTV footage recovered from the school coupled
with enhanced review at the Forensic Imaging and Acoustic Laboratory at DCI
National Police Service Forensics Laboratory, a positive identification of the
students who lit the fire has been realized
Further analysis of the CCTV footage, conducted in collaboration with the
teachers, has enabled the investigation team to confirm the identity of seven
students who participated in the arson before escaping the scene. Of the eight
suspects previously arrested, six have been positively identified and confirmed
through the footage. The seventh identified student was among those earlier
released to their parents and is currently not in custody. Efforts are now
underway to trace and arrest her.
Meanwhile, the post-mortem examinations of the sixteen deceased students were
conducted at Naivasha Sub-County Referral Hospital Mortuary by a team of
pathologists led by Dr. Dorothy Njeri. The examinations confirmed that all
sixteen students died as a result of severe burns. While at the hospital, the Kenya
Red Cross teams provided psychosocial support to the bereaved families, who
were allowed to view the bodies of their loved ones. DNA reference samples were
---
also collected from the families of the deceased students to facilitate formal
identification of the remains which was necessitated by the extent of the burns.
The National Police Service reiterates its deepest condolences to the bereaved
families, relatives, friends, and the entire school community. We also wish quick
recovery to those still receiving medical treatment.
The DCI thanks members of the public, parents, guardians, students and the
school community for their continued calm, patience, and full cooperation with
the investigating team during this difficult period. We particularly appreciate the
parents and students who have actively assisted the investigators by providing
statements and supporting the review of evidence. We urge anyone with
additional information that may assist the on-going investigation to continue
coming forward.
The DCI remains committed to conducting a thorough, professional, and
impartial inquiry to deliver justice for the victims and their families.
Further updates will be provided as more developments emerge.
J. K. MARETE, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
MAY 31, 2026.

PRESS RELEASE
INVESTIGATION UPDATE- INQUIRY INTO THE DEATH OF HON. CYRUS JIRONGO
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) has commenced investigations into
the circumstances surrounding the death of Hon. Cyrus Jirongo, who succumbed to
injuries sustained in a fatal road traffic accident that occurred on the night of 13th
December 2025 at the Karai area along the Nakuru-Nairobi Highway.
Preliminary investigations reveal that the accident involved Hon. Jirongo's motor
vehicle, registration number KCZ 305U, and a public service vehicle (PSV) bus,
registration number KCU 576A, belonging to Climax Company Ltd. The collision
occurred at approximately 02:19 A.M., resulting in a head-on impact that pushed the
deceased's vehicle about 25 metres from the point of impact, while the PSV bus came
to a stop approximately 50 metres away.
In line with its mandate, the DCI deployed a combined team of homicide detectives
and forensic experts from the National Forensic Laboratory, who visited the scene,
conducted preliminary examinations, and secured key exhibits. During scene
documentation, detectives recovered CCTV footage from Eagol Petrol Station, which
has been subjected to initial review and analysis.
The footage shows that at 02:18:40 A.M., the deceased drove into the petrol station
from the Nairobi direction but did not fuel. At 02:19:10 A.M., he stopped at the
station's exit and, at 02:19:19 A.M., made a right turn, driving back towards the
Nairobi direction. At 02:19:25 A.M., the CCTV captured the PSV bus ramming into
the deceased's vehicle.
Detectives have interrogated the PSV driver, Tyrus Kamau Githinji, who had earlier
recorded a statement at the Naivasha Traffic Base. Tyrus is out on cash bail pending
further investigations into the offence of causing death by dangerous driving. He is
required to report to the Naivasha Traffic Base on 22nd December 2025 for further
police action. Additionally, detectives have interviewed the petrol station's night
guard and fuel attendant, both of whom have provided their personal accounts of the
events that occurred on the fateful night.
---
Investigations are ongoing, with the forensic team scheduled to revisit the scene for
further analysis. Detectives are also examining Hon. Jirongo's movements prior to the
accident, including recording statements from individuals he interacted with on the
night in question, notably those present during a meeting at Karen Oasis Bar and
Restaurant, Nairobi.
Further analysis of the CCTV footage is underway, and additional statements will be
recorded from passengers aboard the Climax Company Ltd bus and other witnesses.
Upon completion, a comprehensive police file will be compiled and forwarded to the
Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) for perusal and advice.
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations conveys its condolences to the family,
friends, and relatives of Hon. Cyrus Jirongo and assures the public of its commitment
to conducting thorough, impartial, and credible investigations in accordance with the
Constitution of Kenya and the rule of law.
J. K. MARETE, HSC
FOR DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
December 16, 2025

OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS STATEMENT
National Police Service Headquarters
For Immediate Release
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE CONDEMNS UNPROFESSIONAL CONDUCT IN
THE ARREST OF A SUSPECT IN NAKURU
The National Police Service (NPS) has noted a video circulating on social media
showing the inappropriate handling of a suspect during an arrest.
The Service strongly condemns all forms of unprofessional conduct, excessive
force, or breaches of established procedures. We remain committed to upholding
the highest standards of professionalism, respect for human rights, and
adherence to the Constitution of Kenya and other relevant laws.
Preliminary reports indicate that the incident occurred on Thursday, 25 June
2026, in Nakuru City and may not have followed the Service's Standard
Operating Procedures or the legal safeguards designed to protect the dignity and
rights of suspects. Such behavior is unacceptable and contrary to the core values
of the National Police Service.
The Inspector General has directed the Internal Affairs Unit to conduct a
thorough, professional, and impartial investigation into the matter within seven
days. Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings.
We urge members of the public to continue cooperating with the police in
maintaining law and order. Anyone with information that may assist the
investigation is encouraged to report to the nearest police station or contact the
emergency numbers 999 or 911, the # FichuaKwaDCI toll-free line 0800 722 203,
or WhatsApp on 0709 570 000.
National Police Service reaffirms its zero-tolerance policy towards brutality,
misconduct, or any actions that undermine public trust. We remain committed
to professional policing that serves and protects all Kenyans, residents, and
visitors while fully respecting their constitutional rights.
MUCHIRNYAGA
DIRECTOR CORPORATE COMMUNICATION/SPOKESPERSON
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
June 26, 2026
End

NATIONAL
SERVICE
POLICE
OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS STATEMENT
For Immediate Release
National Police Service Headquarters, Nairobi
SHOOTING INCIDENT/DEATH OF A POLICE OFFICER AT MAKADARA LAW
COURTS, NAIROBI
The National Police Service wishes to apprise the public about the unfortunate
and highly regrettable shooting incident that happened today June 13, 2024 at
the Makadara Law Courts in 2Nairobi.
Today, at about 1345 hrs, a Presiding Magistrate for Makadara Law Courts (name
withheld) was shot by a suspect later identified as No. 235435 Chief Inspector
Samson Kipchirchir Kipruto, the OCS Londiani Police Station.
Preliminary investigations indicate that the Officer was in the Court for unknown
reasons, during a court session of a case involving one Jennifer Wairimu, who is
accused of obtaining Ksh. 2.9 million by false pretence. Police Court Orderlies
swiftly responded to the distress call and fatally shot the rogue Officer.
Also injured during the incident were two Police Constables who are currently
admitted together with the Magistrate at Metropolitan Hospital in Buruburu for
treatment.
While the Service is yet to establish the circumstances that led to the shooting,
all our specialized teams led by the DCI Homicide Unit are on the ground
conducting in-depth investigation into the incident.
The Inspector General of Police takes this early opportunity to reassure the
Judiciary of the safety of all their Staff as they discharge their noble duty.
The National Police Service further reiterates its commitment to protect life and
property of all Kenyans and the many foreign visitors alike.
IG JAPHET KOOME, MGH, EBS, HSC, ndc (K)
INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE &
PRESIDENT OF AFRIPOL GENERAL ASSEMBLY
June 13, 2024

text:
CRIMINALS ON THE RUN
The following individuals are part of the
gang that attacked and killed a teacher and
police officer at Mahero area in Siaya
County on 20th November 2023. The
officials were part of the team that was
invigilating and supervising the Kenya
Certificate of Secondary Education
examination. The individuals escaped the
police dragnet at Nina village on 22nd
November 2023. The National Police
Service is appealing to members of the
public to share any information to the
nearest police station or through the free
hotline number 0800722203 to report
anonymously about the presence of the
individuals in their localities. The police
are also extending their investigations to
the neighbouring countries and have
already reached out to the INTERPOL to
assist to apprehend the suspects.
---
1.
WANTED
EDWARD WANYAMA
MUKANGA alias RAMADHAN
MUKANGA alias ABU NAIYAH
He hails from Mung'ao B village in Gangu
Location within Siaya County and he was
a fisherman at Ogangara beach. Edward is
the leader of the criminal gang based in
Hawinga area in Siaya County and the
mastermind of the plot to attack the
teacher and police officer on the material
day.
---
2. EDWIN OMONDI alias RASHID
The individual hails from Hawinga area
within Uranga in Siaya County. He is a
member of the criminal gang that is
responsible for the series of attacks within
Siaya, Kisumu and Busia counties.
---
WANTED
3. SIMON OCHIENG OUMA alias ALI BABA alias HASSAN alias OBAS
Simon is a resident of Uhuyi area within Uranga in Siaya County. He is also linked
to criminal activities in Baba Dogo area in Nairobi County.

sh1.3 Billion
drugs haul
By Inspector Mike Mugo
S
ix Pakistani nationals and one
Iranian who were found guilty
of trafficking heroin worth Sh1.3
Billion via the Indian Ocean to
Kenya's coastal city of Mombasa have
been sentenced to life in prison. The seven
had been in custody for 9 years since 2014
when they were arrested and charged
with trafficking 377 kilograms of granular
heroin, 33,200 liters of liquid heroin and
2,100 liters of diesel mixed with heroin.
In a ruling delivered by Mombasa Chief
Magistrate Martha Mutuku on March 10,
2023, the seven sailors were fined Sh3.9
billion, thrice the value of the heroin they
trafficked, and in default to paying the
fine, they shall serve one year in prison.
The seven were crew members of a ship
Amin Darya, also known as Al Noor, and
were arrested while the ship was sailing
in the Kenyan territorial waters along the
Indian Ocean by Kenya Navy personnel
on patrol. They are Yousuf Yakoob,
Yakoob Ibrahim, Saleem Muhammad,
Bhatti Abdul Ghafour, Baksh Moula, Pak
Abdolghaffer and Muhammed Saleh.
This was a classical case of trafficking
by conveying Narcotic drugs, contrary to
section (a) of the Narcotics drugs and
psychotropic substances control Act No. 4
of 1994. On November 12, 2013 one Vikas
son of Balwan and Praveen Prabhakaran
Nair, both Indian Nationals, left Mumbai
aboard Air India A1983 destined for Dubai.

worked on that ship and sailed to various
destinations including Kuwait, Dubai among
others. While in the Gulf the ship would carry
white cement and other goods.
The following year on April 21, 2014, the
6 Pakistanis who were convicted met the
two Indian nationals and one Iranian Pak
Abdolghaffar also a convict, and the owner
of the ship whom detectives identified
as Ahemed Mohammad. The ship owner

to Iran via

119 small bags and 28 bags of 50kilograms
of white cement 9(super plaster). All the
above mentioned were partly removed and
stored in a warehouse next to berth No. 8 and
the process of physical verification of the
contents commenced till late in the night.
The search continued until July 7, 2014, when
at around 12 noon, a package of some whitish
substance was recovered by detectives on
the portside rail of the ship in the cargo deck
fore end. The ship's captain Yousuf Yaqoob
and the ship engineer Saleh Muhammad
witnessed the recovery. On July 8, 2014, the
suspected drug substance was escorted to
the Government Chemist based in Mombasa
for weighing and sampling. The weight was
found to be 974 grams, and a preliminary test
on the substance tested positive for heroin,
in an exercise witnessed by the captain
of the ship and other two crew members.
The following day, 787 empty packets were
recovered from ballast tanks in the vessel.
The packets were all slit on one side. They
were found stashed in 16 bags after ripping
off the bottom of the cargo deck and traces of
substance believed to be narcotic drugs were
also found in them.
By July 11, 2014, a total of 166 drums of 200
liters filled with brownish liquid substance
that was recovered from the ballast tested
positive for heroin. In a shocking revelation,
the highly addictive drug had also been
concealed in over 2,100 litres of diesel
contained in drums in the reservoir. In total,
all the solid substance recovered was 377.221
kilograms of heroin valued at Sh1,131,672,000.
Over 33,200 litres from the ballast water and
2,100 litres of diesel laced with heroin were
also recovered in one of the biggest drugs

case reported in the country's history. Further
investigations revealed that the declared
cargo, super plaster amounting to 300 metric
tons was not discharged at the port specified
for discharge in Dubai as reflected on the bill
of lading. Instead, the vessel sailed towards an
unspecified destination only to end up along
the Kenyan territorial waters. The vessel had
been registered in Iran as M/V Amin Darya,
however in the general export manifest, the
same vessel was indicated as AL. NOOR 1082.
However, on the same general export manifest
as a risk indicator, it was noted that Mombasa
was the "Port of Loading" and Kenya the "Port
of Destination." As investigations continued,
detectives established that between July 2 to
July 3, 2014, one day before the vessel was
intercepted, one Khalid Agil Ahmed (who
was arrested later) a manager with Blue Bay
Shipping Agency had communicated with
the alleged owner of the ship via a cell phone
number registered in Dubai six times while
the vessel was still sailing into Kenyan waters.
Besides the recovery of documentary
evidence, when the officers conducted
search on the vessel, an exercise book was
also recovered from the deputy captain
of the ship that bore a hand written cell
phone number 0722-710 7xx and the name
"Khaled, Mombaso". Another suspect
Mohamed Osman Ahmed the operations
Manager of Zam Zam Shipping Agency, who
was also arrested later, was found to have
communicated with the alleged owner of
M/V Amin Darya. This was after detectives
recovered a piece of paper from the vessel's
captain bearing his cell phone number. A copy
of an email exchange indicating that there

The National Police Service (NPS) wishes to inform the public of a heinous attack carried out by
suspected militia earlier today, 9th May 2026, along the Mandera-Arabia Road.
A Nissan matatu, registration number KAQ 914S, hired to transport family members to Arabia
Town, came under indiscriminate fire from suspected militia shortly after passing the Omar Jillo
Centre.
Upon receiving the distress call, a multi-agency security team responded swiftly. The team
immediately facilitated the evacuation of the injured to Arabia Sub-County Level Four Hospital.
Tragically, six victims were pronounced dead on arrival. Three others sustained serious injuries;
they have been stabilised and transferred to Mandera County Referral Hospital, where they are
receiving further specialised medical care.
The National Police Service extends its deepest condolences to the families, friends and loved ones
of the deceased. We pray for a full and speedy recovery for the injured, who remain under medical
care.
A multi-agency team, including specialised units, remains actively deployed in the area, where a
comprehensive search and pursuit operation is underway with the sole aim of hunting down the
perpetrators. We are committed to bringing them to justice and ensuring they face the full force of
the law.
We encourage anyone with information that may assist the investigation to contact the nearest
police station, use the toll free numbers 999, 911 or provide information anonymously via
#FichuaKwaDCI on 0800 722 203 or WhatsApp 0709 570 000.
The National Police Service wishes to assure residents of the area, and indeed the entire nation,
that we remain resolute in our constitutional mandate to protect life and property. We will not be
cowed by such cowardly acts of violence. Further updates will be provided as the operation
progresses.
MUCHIRI YAGA

Who is a Homicide Detective and
what do Homicide Detectives Do?
A homicide detective is a specialized law enforcement officer
dedicated to investigating and solving attempted homicides and
homicides. He or she must be very intelligent, unusually clever
and observant, but also unpredictable. We investigate murders
and try to solve many of the mysteries surrounding unexplained
deaths.
By working closely with general duty officers, forensic experts
including experts from the Government Pathologist and
Government Chemist, homicide detectives diligently uncover
the details and circumstances surrounding a crime while
utilizing their expertise to bring justice to victims and their
families. When a suspicious death is reported, detectives from
various units including Homicide, Crime Scene Investigations,
Photographic & Acoustics, and Digital forensics among others
evaluate the crime scene. This is because the expectations are
very high since the suspects involved are to be charged with very
serious offences.
Conducting investigations is the bulk of any homicide
detective's work. This often starts at the scene of the crime.
Some detectives work on cases that are years or decades
old, which makes visiting the original scene impossible. A
lot of the work comes in terms of following clues, piecing
together event sequences, and trying to nail down what,
exactly, happened when the victim or victims died.
Interviews with witnesses, if there are any, are also a very
important element, and the victim's friends and relatives
may also be questioned. Also, paperwork, including going
back through the victim's diary, receipts, Mpesa Statements
and phone records etc is also very essential. By so doing,
the detective is basically trying to reconstruct the days and
hours leading up to the death of the victim.
Evidence Collection
The select team of detectives also looks for evidence that
can lead to the arrest or at least identification of the main
suspect or other accomplices to the crime. This can include
blood samples and measurements taken from the crime
scene to artifacts found in the victim's home or scene of
crime. A good homicide detective has to not only know
what to look for, but also understand how to collect and
store evidence so that it can be admissible in court. Our judicial
system has strict guidelines about how evidence is collected and
handled so that there isn't any confusion about its validity or
significance.
However, not all of the detective's work is done in the field, and
most of the major breakthroughs that happen come about as a
result of deep thought and logical reasoning While Homicide
detectives must be skilled at investigation and evidence
collection, these efforts may become futile if the investigator
fails to piece his or her findings together in a convincing and
meaningful manner. He or she must follow his or her instincts
and take the time to think through the many pieces of the puzzle.
This can often be very frustrating and slow.
Logical Reasoning
Not all of our work is done in the field, and actually, most of the
major breakthroughs that we have had in the past come about as
a result of deep thought and logical reasoning. While Homicide
detectives must be skilled at investigation and evidence
collection, these efforts don't mean much if the investigator
can't piece his or her findings together in a convincing and
meaningful way. He or she must follow his or her instincts
and take time to think through the many pieces of the puzzle.
Sometimes it can often be very frustrating and slow.
The main goal is always to solve the case by identifying what Testimony
happened, how it happened, and who is responsible. Interviewing
witnesses, collecting evidence, and going through the facts
available is also at the core of our work.Homicide detectives
are more experienced and well rounded in interviewing, case
analysis and file management since most of our cases are of
higher profile than other criminal cases. In summary our work
can be classified as follows.
In the event that a homicide detective's findings lead to an arrest
or conviction, he or she may be summoned to testify in court or
provide other statements of the case and its facts. Courts depend
on a detective's testimony to help magistrates and judges make
sense of what occurred. Testimony is frequently made in person,
and written statements are always also required.

major breakthroughs that we have had in the past come about as
a result of deep thought and logical reasoning. While Homicide
detectives must be skilled at investigation and evidence
collection, these efforts don't mean much if the investigator
can't piece his or her findings together in a convincing and
meaningful way. He or she must follow his or her instincts
and take time to think through the many pieces of the puzzle.
Sometimes it can often be very frustrating and slow.
The main goal is always to solve the case by identifying what Testimony
happened, how it happened, and who is responsible. Interviewing
witnesses, collecting evidence, and going through the facts
available is also at the core of our work.Homicide detectives
are more experienced and well rounded in interviewing, case
analysis and file management since most of our cases are of
higher profile than other criminal cases. In summary our work
can be classified as follows.
In the event that a homicide detective's findings lead to an arrest
or conviction, he or she may be summoned to testify in court or
provide other statements of the case and its facts. Courts depend
on a detective's testimony to help magistrates and judges make
sense of what occurred. Testimony is frequently made in person,
and written statements are always also required.

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
PRESS STATEMENT
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
STATEMENT ON THE ARREST OF GRACE NDUTA WAIRIMU
The attention of the Directorate of Criminal Investigations has been drawn to reports
circulating on social media on alleged abduction of Grace Nduta Wairimu. We wish to
confirm that Grace Nduta Wairimu, MCA representing Kanyenya-ini ward in
Murang'a County, was arrested today May 29, 2025 as part of an ongoing investigation
on the stage-managed abduction of Hon George Koimburi.
It has been confirmed that, despite her claims of being in Kangema and attending
church services and political rallies on May 25, 2025, evidence clearly shows that she
was at the Ellis Bar and Restaurant in Kiganjo, Gatundu South, with Hon. George
Koimburi the entire night.
Further updates will be shared as the investigation continues.
John Marete, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
May 29, 2025

Gun-toting desperados neutralized in
gunfire showdown with anti-robbery
detectives
By Chief Inspector Jonah Kimani
5
2
.
5
r
1
r

r
.
Jour armed robbers who were
on police radar for staging
and executing a string of
armed robberies in Machakos,
Mombasa and Kwale Counties since
2021 were shot dead on June 12, 2023 in
a fierce exchange of fire with detectives.
The stealth raid was conducted at a
small village of Takaungu in Kilifi
County, at a house where the daredevil
gang had regrouped to stage more
attacks. After being surrounded, they
had defied orders to surrender and
instead challenged a select team of
crack shot officers to a duel by firing
frenziedly at them. Unbeknownst to
them, the sleuths had been trailing
them for months and were sharpening
their claws each passing day, ready for
any eventuality that could see a police
rifle earlier robbed from a bank guard
recovered.
street-fight and the smell of gun powder.
It had been operating with the impudence
of a stray stallion, perhaps to stamp its rise
among the underworld as an unstoppable
ruffian gang. And indeed, the scorch of
its heat was felt by its target counties.
Police came to learn of the gang in July 27,
2021 when it staged a bank heist at Equity
bank in Matuu, Machakos County and
made away with an undisclosed amount
of money. This was after they disarmed
a female police officer who was on guard
duties and took off with her AK-47 rifle
serial number KE KP 5527115, that was
loaded with 30 rounds of ammunition.
As local police responded in an effort
to avert the robbery, the gang fired
indiscriminately and made good its
escape. It was a gang of five. Since then,
the miscreants terrorized Kenyans in
over 10 armed robberies through brazen
In the night. The miscreants terrorized Kenyans
• the quietness
1
ら
of the sleepy in over 10 armed robberies through
coastal creek
was suddenly brazen attacks
interrupted
by rattling
gunfire, as the sleuths drawn from the
elite Crime Research & Intelligence
Bureau augmented by the Operations
Support Unit answered to the thugs
provocation with precision. When the
guns went silent, four male robbers lay
down dead and cold, after bullet shots
ripped through their hideout felling
them in their own game of choice.
But the audacious ring was not new to
attacks, targeting Mpesa shops and other
business establishments in Mombasa and
Kwale counties. A comprehensive forensic
analysis conducted at the DCI National
Forensic Laboratory linked the lost police
firearm to two suspects, one only identified
as Festus and the other as Tsuma Ndoro.
A team of highly skilled detectives was
immediately deployed with orders to go
after the thugs, stop the robbery spree and
---
The DCI
CRIME WATCH
EQUITY
Equity Bank Matuu branch that was robbed by a
five-member gang on July, 2021.
AK47 rifle robbed from bank-guard police during the
daring raid at Equity bank Matuu on July, 2021. It was
recovered in Takaungu, Kilifi.
recover the stolen government rifle. After
weeks of trailing the gang that had since
taken cover in Kwale county, their efforts
paid off when the thugs made a move and
crossed the Likoni channel on June 12.The
sleuths trailed them stealthily from Likoni
ferry to Shimanzi, Nyali and Shariani,
before finally cornering them in Takaungu
moments to midnight. The miscreants
were believed to have been planning a
mega robbery Kilifi town. The tales of the
events that unfolded that night will remain
registered in the minds of Takaungu
residents, who were unfortunately placed
in the middle of the deadly operation.
Luckily, no untargeted subject was injured
as even the police escaped unscathed.
The AK-17 assault rifle stolen in the
Matuu Equity bank heist was recovered,
loaded with only seven rounds of the 30
live ammunitions that had been loaded.
In the operation, two motorcycles make
Boxer KMFS 63IT and Haogin KMEF 182P
that were being used by the suspects as
getaway means were also impounded.
As news of the successful mission made
rounds on various reporting outlets, the
investigating team sharpened its tools on
yet another suspect who remained in the
shadows. This one was more dangerous,
more experienced and slippery. According
to the intelligence information available
to them, he was an
equally good shooter.
and was believed to have
disagreed with the ring leader on who
was to handle the AK 17 rifle, thereby
separating with a promise of making a
loud return.
His name was Joseph Kariuki Ruoro, an
ex-police officer who previously served in
the General Service Unit. The blackguard.
who could not live up to the oath of office
for police officers had tucked away after
most of his accomplices were either
arrested or fell by the gun in various
Ex-GSU officer arrested in Gilgil,
Nakuru county in connection with the
Matuu robbery.
robbery encounters with police. His name
had become particularly apparent after
the Equity Bank Matuu robbery incident
which he was believed to have planned.
When he therefore missed in the list of the
neutralized gang in Kilifi, detectives knew
that there were still more accomplices on
the loose. Hence, the operation could not
be called off.
The DCI has remained steadfast to
sanitize the streets of gangsters and
scrupulously hunt for guns in the wrong
hands. This particular case was not going
to be any different. In fact, preliminary
investigations had so far linked Ruoro to
9 robbery incidents reported in Mombasa,
Kwale, Kilifi and Machakos counties, most
of which he staged with the slain gang.
Detectives later flushed Ruoro out of his
hideout in Gilgil, Nakuru county on July,
2023 and charged him in court. He is
currently hanging by the skin of his teeth
as he battles violent robbery charges that
could see him sentenced to death. But
the path of the Matuu bank heist gang is
not the only one that has hit a cul de sac.
A spate of violent robberies has equally
rocked the Western and North Rift regions,
with police hotly pursuing the perpetrators
day in day out. One such case is the May
22, 2023 arrest of two suspects believed
to be behind armed attacks on innocent
AUGUST | 2023
71
---
civilians in Kakamega, Vihiga and Uasin-
Gishu Counties. Detectives drawn from
Crime Research & Intelligence Bureau
arrested the two suspects in Kakamega,
following a chase that culminated at river
Lwatingu where the main suspect intended
to plunge into the waters to evade justice.
The unit had deployed several undercover
sleuths at various streets and drinking
joints in Kakamega, before making their
final move that also led to the recovery of
a firearm.
The two suspects, Patrick Mangale, 30
and Denis Indeche, 24, had masterminded
several armed robberies in the county.
including the April 9, 2023 attack on a
senior DCI officer. The bloodthirsty duo
had hacked the officers head several times
in cold blood, leaving him for the dead. On
the fateful night, the officer who is based
at DCI Kakamega north had just arrived
at his residence gate at around 3am from
an assignment in Nairobi. The two thugs
who rode on a motorbike accosted him,
descending on him with a machete thus
inflicting several deep cuts on his head.
After the heinous act, they vanished into
the darkness with his Jericho pistol loaded
with 15 rounds of ammunition. Armed with
the stolen firearm, the thugs abandoned
machetes as their weapons of choice.
embarking on a robbery spree that targeted
Mpesa shops and pump stations. On April
11, 2023 at around 9:30pm, the duo staged
an attack at Aziz petrol station in Shibuli
shopping centre within Kakamega county
where they left with an unknown amount
of money. Two days later, they attacked a
gold dealer in Lwanugu village where they
ordered everyone at the gold mining site
to lie down. They had then taken off with
Sh55,000, several grams of gold, mobile
phones and other valuables. In yet another
incident on April 20, at around 10pm, the
gun-toting thugs raided an Mpesa shop at
Mudete market in Maragoli and took off
with an unspecified amount of money and
mobile phones. On sensing that detectives
had launched a manhunt for them in
Western Kenya, the miscreants who were
lucky to escape several police dragnets
fled to Uasin Gishu County, where they
continued with their activities targeting
shops and other businesses.
In one of the attacks, two innocent
civilians suffered gunshot injuries on their
hands and legs, as the thugs raided a shop
at Elgon View estate in Eldoret and made
away with cash. Several detachments of
the police were mobilized and the two
suspects arrested. Upon interrogation.
the main suspect (Patrick Mangale) led
the officers to a toilet at his homestead in
Lower Tingu, Mugulu area in Kakamega
county, where the firearm loaded with
two rounds of 9mm calibre was recovered
hidden in a pit latrine. The detectives also
impounded a motorcycle registration
number KMGG 121M believed to have
been the gang's getaway means.
This was a huge win by police against
armed criminals, a testament of the cliché
"Mkono mrefu wa serikali". But even
before the suspects could take plea in court.
one of the two suspects (Denis Indeche)
alongside another escaped from Kakamega
Police Station in unclear circumstances.
This was a set-back to his ultimate
justice and a let-down to the undercover
detectives who had braved very unfamiliar
grounds for weeks to bring to an end the
era of impunity, terror and lawlessness by
the criminal duo.Consequently, two police
officers who were on duty when the two
escaped were placed in custody to assist
with investigations, with their careers
hanging in the balance should charges of
aiding the escape be proven.
But no force is as unstoppable as that of
police hell-bent to put criminals where
they belong. It was just a matter of time
before the escapees could be ushered
back as guests of the state. And indeed,
this happened three days later when Denis
Indeche was swept from a changȧa den
where the spirits of those he had terrorized
were haunting him. Interestingly, he was
arrested in a normal security patrol by
Malaika Police Station officers, alongside
a fellow Changaa boozer who was hosting
him at his house. Once at the police
station, Indeche had had problems giving
his identity for booking into the cells,
raising curiosity and more suspicion that
he was more than just a toper.His heart
sunk moments later when familiar faces
from Kakamega Police Station arrived at
his Malaika cell and booked his transfer.
to the same facility he had escaped from.
He had added another count in his list of
violent robberies, that of escaping from
lawful custody. As the suspects continue
fighting for a second lease of freedom at
the mercy of the unforgiving law, police
have intensified a manhunt for lawless.
gunmen out to terrorize and rob peace-
loving Kenyans.
AUGUST | 2023

NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
PRESS STATEMENT
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) has noted with grave concern - the
alleged non-consensual recording and subsequent circulation of intimate videos
involving Kenyan women by a suspected Russian national.
The DCI strongly condemns these reported acts, which constitute serious violations of
privacy, personal dignity, and the rights of victims as enshrined in the Constitution of
Kenya. Such conduct also amounts to technology-facilitated gender-based violence,
exploitation, and potential offences under the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act,
the Penal Code, and other relevant statutes protecting women and children.
As the premier investigative agency in the country, the DCI has initiated a
comprehensive inquiry into the matter. This includes: Immediate activation of
specialized cybercrime and gender-based violence investigation units to gather
evidence, trace digital footprints, and identify the suspect, Coordination with
international law enforcement partners and relevant foreign authorities, given the
cross-border elements involved and Pursuit of any individuals or entities involved in
the recording, dissemination, or further circulation of the harmful content.
The DCI urges the affected individuals, victims or witnesses to come forward and
record statements at the DCI headquarters. All statements will be handled with the
utmost confidentiality, dignity, sensitivity, and respect for the privacy and well-being
of the complainants.
Members of the public are reminded that sharing, reposting, or further circulating
such non-consensual intimate content perpetuates secondary victimization and may
attract criminal liability under Kenyan law.
The DCI remains committed to upholding justice, protecting vulnerable persons, and
ensuring accountability in both physical and digital spaces. We will work tirelessly
with all relevant government agencies, stakeholders, and international counterparts
to bring those responsible to justice and prevent future occurrences.
We urge members of the public to remain vigilant and to report such criminalities to
the DCI via #FichuaKwaDCI toll free number 0800 722 203 or via WhatsApp on
0709 570 000.
John Marete, HSC

NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
WANTED SUSPECT
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations is appealing to members of the public for
information that may lead to the arrest of Elizaphan Mayenga Michira, whose
photograph appears below, in connection with investigations into allegations of
obtaining money by false pretences. The suspect is alleged to have posed as a person
capable of facilitating employment opportunities and travel to Canada, targeting job
seekers with promises of positions including Nurse Aides, storekeepers and truck
drivers.
He is further alleged to have demanded substantial sums of money from prospective
applicants, purportedly to cater for visa processing, medical examinations, biometrics
and air travel. Investigations established that some of the documents and travel
arrangements presented to the complainants by the suspect were fraudulent. The matter
has since been registered before the Milimani Law Courts under CR No. 011/14/2026
and Criminal Case No. E223/2026, where a warrant of arrest has been issued and
remains in force.
Michira is currently at large, and detectives have intensified efforts to trace and
apprehend him.
PARTICULARS
Name: Elizaphan Mayenga Michira
District: Borabu
Division: Borabu
Location: Makenene
Sub-Location: Matutu
Elizaphan Mayenga Michira
Members of the public who may have information regarding his whereabouts, or any
information that could assist in his arrest, are urged to report to the nearest police
station or anonymously through #FichuaKwaDCI. Call 0800 722 203 (Toll-Free) or
WhatsApp 0709 570 000. All information received will be treated with the utmost
confidentiality.

text:
WANTED SIAYA GANG LEADER ARRESTED
Police in Nairobi have arrested a wanted criminal gang leader who was on the run
following a tip of from members of the public. Edward Wanyama
Mukanga aka Ramadhan Mukanga alias Abu Naiyah, 34 was the leader of the
gang and a mastermind of the Siaya attack, where a police officer was killed and
another one was injured and robbed off of their rifles as they escorted
examination papers to Mahero Secondary School in Alego Usonga Sub-County in
Siaya County on 20th November 2023.
Edward was arrested while in a hideout within Nairobi's Dandora slum on Friday
26th January 2024. Earlier, the police had published names and photos of Abu
Naiyah and his associates including Edwin Omondi alias Rashid, Simon Ochieng
Ouma alias Ali Baba, Salim Jackoyo, and Hasting Omondi on the media and
appealed to members of the public to share any information on their
whereabouts.
The National Police Service appreciates the swift action by members of the
public that has so far led to the arrest of Hasting Omondi who was apprehended
in Usenge Village within the Bondo area of Siaya County in December 2023. The
suspect was presented in Kahawa Law Courts on Monday 29th January 2024
where detectives were granted 25 days to complete their investigation.
National Police Service is urging the remaining gang members to surrender to the
nearest police station. At the same time, members of the public are urged share
any information on other wanted persons to the nearest police station or through
the toll-free number 0800722203.

OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS STATEMENT
National Police Service Headquarters
For Immediate Release
NPS COMMENCES INVESTIGATION INTO ALLEGED MASS GRAVE DISCOVERY IN
KERICHO COUNTY
Following the alleged discovery of a mass grave within the Makaburini Cemetery in
Kericho County, and in line with our mandate, officers from the National Police Service in
Kericho promptly visited and secured the scene to preserve the integrity of potential
evidence.
At this preliminary stage, we are seeking to establish the veracity of the claims. Some
witnesses have since recorded statements, and efforts are underway to locate and
interview more persons of interest in this matter.
The National Police Service assures the public that this matter is being handled with the
utmost seriousness and will be conducted professionally and transparently to ascertain
the facts surrounding this incident.
We appeal to members of the public to remain calm as investigations are ongoing. Any
person with information that may assist this investigation is requested to report to the
nearest police station or law enforcement officer, or to share it via our toll-free numbers:
999, 911, 112, or anonymously via our #FichuakwaDCI on 0800 722 203 or WhatsApp
0709 570 000.
The National Police Service remains resolute in conducting impartial, thorough and
expedient investigations in accordance with the law. Further updates will be provided as
the investigation progresses.
MUCHIRI NYAGA
DIRECTOR CORPORATE COMMUNICATION/SPOKESPERSON
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
March 22, 2026
Ends

1. JULIUS MUTUA JOHN was arrested in JOSKA after stealing a
TOYOTA ALLION KDR 722K.

motor vehicles through a car hire scheme. He collaborates with
Suspect No. 1
3. ALPHAS KIMAIGA MOGAKA. He is an expert at removing car
trackers from stolen vehicles.
4. SIMON MUGO CHEGE. He is an expert at erasing a car's
identity. He collaborates with a car theft syndicate, assisting
them in removing any trace of the vehicle's original identity.
5. RAPHAEL OLOO KIRA alias Cease Fire. He fabricates
counterfeit car number plates and affixes them to stolen
vehicles after removing their original, legitimate plates.

On April 8, 2025, a team raided the yard, where stolen vehicles'
chassis numbers had been altered and put up for sale to
unsuspecting buyers. She receives a commission for each vehicle
sold. During the raid, the team recovered several vehicles.

motor vehicles.

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
PRESS RELEASE
FURTHER UPDATE- INQUIRY INTO THE DEATH OF HON. CYRUS JIRONGO
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) wishes to update the public on the
ongoing investigations into the tragic death of Hon. Cyrus Jirongo, which occurred on
the night of 13th December 2025 at Karai area along the Nakuru-Nairobi Highway.
Following the incident, the DCI promptly launched thorough investigations to establish
the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. A multi-disciplinary team, comprising
Homicide detectives, experts from the Crime Research and Intelligence Bureau, and
forensic specialists from the National Forensic Laboratory, was deployed.
The team visited and processed the scene, secured and preserved key exhibits,
documented physical evidence, and recovered CCTV footage from Eagol Petrol Station
for review and analysis. Additionally, the bus manifest and amateur videos from the
scene were obtained and subjected to forensic analysis.
Furthermore, the investigative team recorded statements from several key witnesses,
including Mrs. Ann Lanoi Pertet, the deceased's wife and the first family member
contacted after the incident; Mr. Tiras Kamau Githinji, the driver of the ill-fated bus;
Mr. Manoah Ekokwa Alukoya Olasi, the bus conductor; and staff members from Eagol
petrol station. Additionally, Rt. Hon. Moses Wetang'ula, Mr. Rebman Malala, and Mr.
Ibrahim Sambuli-who had an interaction with the deceased at Karen Oasis restaurant
in the evening of 12th December, 2025-voluntarily came forward to provide the
investigators with their accounts of the events.
Further, seven passengers from the ill-fated bus presented themselves to assist in the
investigation, and their statements were also recorded. The detectives also recorded a
statement from Julius Kiprotich Chelule, the driver of the alleged rescue bus Reg. No.
KCU 573A.
Based on the evidence gathered and analysed to date, the incident appears to be a road
traffic accident, with no indications of foul play. Upon conclusion of the remaining
investigative processes, the investigation file will be forwarded to the Office of the
Director of Public Prosecutions (ODPP) for appropriate directions, including potential
criminal charges against the PSV driver, in line with the available evidence.
---
The DCI extends deepest condolences to the family, relatives and friends of Hon. Cyrus
Jirongo.
We urge the public and political leaders to exercise restraint and refrain from making
speculative or unsubstantiated statements that could prejudice the investigative process
or cause undue public anxiety. Any person who possesses information that they believe
may assist the ongoing investigations is encouraged to come forward and contact the
nearest police station or the Directorate of Criminal Investigations through
#FichuaKwaDCI 0800722203 (Toll-free) or WhatsApp at 0709570000 to report
anonymously.
The DCI remains resolute in conducting impartial, thorough and expedient
investigations in accordance with the law.
J. K. MARETE, HSC
FOR DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
JANUARY 5, 2026

NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
National Police Service Headquarters
For Immediate Release
PRESS STATEMENT
NPS CONDEMNS SERIOUS PETROL ATTACK ON A WOMAN IN MWIKI AND TWO PHYSICAL ASSAULTS
ON TRAFFIC OFFICERS IN LANG'ATA AND EMBAKASI
The National Police Service (NPS) strongly condemns three incidents reported within the past 24 hours in the
Nairobi region.
In the first incident, which occurred yesterday, 16th May 2026, in the Mwiki area of Kasarani Sub-county, a
woman is fighting for her life at Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) after being doused with what is believed to
be petrol and set alight. Preliminary investigations suggest that the attack was linked to the woman's political
views, which allegedly displeased her attackers. The matter is being investigated by a specialised team from
the DCI Headquarters.
The second incident involves a video circulating widely on social media, showing a motorist confronting and
physically assaulting a traffic police officer on duty in the Embakasi area. The motorist has been identified,
and due process is underway.
The third incident took place in the Lang'ata area, where the crew of a Metro Shuttle bus attacked a traffic
officer who was enforcing the law. The crew were swiftly arrested, and the bus has been impounded.
NPS condemns all three incidents in the strongest possible terms. Political intolerance has no place in
competitive politics, our democracy, or our laws. Furthermore, any attack-whether verbal, physical, or
otherwise against a police officer is an affront to the rule of law and undermines the integrity and dignity of
the National Police Service. Such attacks are an assault on our collective freedom.
National Police Service commends the officers involved for their restraint, professionalism, and composure in
the face of intense provocation. We continue to remind the public to support lawfully engaged officers who
remain dedicated to their mandate, while calling for enhanced community engagement and collaboration.
Mutual respect between the police and the public remains fundamental to a peaceful and orderly society.
The Service will not hesitate to take firm and appropriate lawful action against anyone who undermines police
authority or attempts to impede officers in the discharge of their duties.
Anyone with further information regarding the incidents described is urged to report to the nearest police
station, a law enforcement officer, or via our toll-free numbers (999, 911), or anonymously through
#FichuaKwaDCI on 0800 722 203 or WhatsApp 0709 570 000.
NPS reiterates its unwavering commitment to upholding the rule of law, ensuring public safety, and respecting
the rights of all citizens, residents, and visitors, while remaining steadfast in its mission to serve, protect, and
maintain law and order across the country with professionalism and integrity.
MUCHIRI NAGA
DIRECTOR CORPORATE COMMUNICATION/SPOKESPERSON
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
May 17, 2026
Ends

OFFICE OF THE INSPECTOR GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
PRESS STATEMENT
National Police Service Headquarters
For Immediate Release
SECURITY BREACH IN GANZE, KILIFI COUNTY
The National Police Service wishes to address a serious security breach that occurred today, 24
May 2026, during a thanksgiving event in Ganze, Kilifi County, where His Excellency Dr. William
Samoei Ruto, President of the Republic of Kenya, was addressing members of the public.
Although security agencies responded swiftly and decisively to contain the situation and restore
order, any breach involving the security of the President is unacceptable and a matter of the
gravest national concern.
As the Inspector General of the National Police Service, I have immediately constituted a special
investigations team to conduct a swift, thorough, and uncompromising inquiry into how this
breach occurred. I have also ordered immediate changes to the security detail responsible for the
President's protection in order to strengthen protocols and seal any existing vulnerabilities.
The security of the Head of State is a matter of national security and will be treated with the
utmost seriousness. We wish to make it clear that all persons attending public events, particularly
those involving the President and other national leaders, must strictly adhere to established
security procedures and protocols at all times. Any attempt to breach security will be met with the
full force of the law.
The National Police Service remains resolute in its constitutional duty to serve and protect the
people of Kenya. We will take every necessary measure to ensure such an incident is never
repeated and that the highest standards of security are maintained for the President, national
leadership, and the nation.
DOUGLAS KANJA KIROCHO, MGH, CBS, OGW
INSPECTOR-GENERAL
NATIONAL POLICE SERVICE
May 24, 2026
Ends

DIRECTORATE OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS
PRESS RELEASE
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
INVESTIGATION INTO FIRE INCIDENT AT UTUMISHI GIRLS SENIOR SECONDARY
SCHOOL IN GILGIL
The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) has launched an in-depth
investigation into the tragic fire incident that occurred on Thursday, May 28, 2026, at
Utumishi Girls Senior Secondary School in Gilgil, Nakuru County, in which sixteen
students lost their lives.
Following the successful conclusion of the multi-agency emergency response and
rescue operations, a dedicated investigation team led by the Director of Homicide has
taken over the case. The emergency response was coordinated by the National Police
Service, with critical support from the NGAO, the Kenya Defence Forces, National
Youth Service, County Government of Nakuru, Kenya Forest Service, State Department
for Children Services, National Disaster Management Unit (NDMU), National Disaster
Operations Centre (NDOC), Kenya Red Cross Society, Department of Public Works,
Kenya Power and Lighting Company (KPLC), Government Chemist, Ministry of
Education officials, medical officers, pathologists, community members, and other key
stakeholders.
The multi-agency investigation team, comprising highly specialized personnel
including Crime Scene Investigators (CSIS), Crime Research & Intelligence Bureau
(CR&IB) officers from the Forensic Imaging and Acoustics Unit, and forensic DNA
experts, has processed the scene at Meline Waithera Dormitory. The dormitory is a
two-storey building in which the first floor sustained extensive fire damage, while the
ground floor remained largely intact. The affected upper floor consists of twelve
cubicles accommodating a total of 135 double-decker beds.
A meticulous examination of the scene led to the recovery of sixteen (16) bodies, all of
which were moved to Naivasha Sub-county Referral Hospital Mortuary pending post-
mortem examinations and formal identification.
---
Crime scene processing and documentation continue today, May 29, 2026, as
investigators work to establish the suspected point of origin of the fire, analyse burn
patterns, identify potential ignition sources, determine the presence of any accelerants,
and evaluate the integrity of electrical installations and structural fire dynamics to
establish the exact cause and sequence of events.
Investigators have conducted extensive interviews with students, teaching staff, and
other witnesses, while forensic teams carry out a detailed review of available CCTV
footage. Preliminary investigations have identified eight students as persons of interest
in connection with the planning and execution of the suspected arson attack. The eight
girls have since been arrested and are currently in police custody. Detectives continue
to record statements and analyse all available evidence to reconstruct the sequence of
events, establish the full circumstances of the incident, and determine the motive.
The National Police Service conveys its deepest condolences to the bereaved families,
relatives, friends, and the entire school community following this heartbreaking
tragedy. We also wish a swift recovery to all those receiving medical treatment.
The DCI acknowledges the profound sensitivity and emotional weight of this incident
and appeals to the public, parents, and guardians for calm, patience, and restraint as
investigations continue. The Directorate assures all stakeholders that a thorough,
professional, and impartial investigation is underway to establish the exact cause and
full circumstances surrounding the fire and to ensure that justice is served, bringing
much-needed closure to the bereaved families and the entire school community.
Further updates will be provided as investigations progress.
John Marete, HSC
FOR: DIRECTOR OF CRIMINAL INVESTIGATIONS.
May 29, 2026
